docs.title: 8. Conclusion
docs.text:
This course has followed, in Dart, exactly the same progression as the [Introduction to the TypeScript language and the NestJS web framework through examples (2026)] course: the fundamentals of the language, functions, four client variations for the same server (a simple script, separate DAO/business layers, a compiled project, and a web application), and database access (MySQL), first via a native driver and then via a hand-written “ORM” driver due to the lack of a mature equivalent to TypeORM or Prisma.

The systematic differences encountered throughout the course highlight Dart’s unique profile compared to TypeScript: NOMINAL and SAIN typing, never contradicted by what actually happens at runtime (no implicit coercion, no MySQL decimal returned as a string despite its declared type); a strict distinction between the Dart world and the JavaScript world when targeting the web ([dart:js_interop], [.toJS]), offset by a AOT compilation that, conversely, does not require a AUCUN polyfill; recent NOUVEAUTÉS features (records, patterns, sealed classes, class modifiers) that play a role in Dart 3 comparable to that of the latest versions of ECMAScript on the TypeScript side; and, finally, a more tightly-knit package ecosystem, where certain tools (ORM and MySQL foremost among them) do not yet have the mature equivalents offered by the npm ecosystem.

docs.title: 7. Database Access
docs.text: The TypeScript course devotes three chapters to accessing a MySQL database: the native driver [mysql2], followed by two ORM ([TypeORM] and [Prisma]), using the same example—two databases, [dbpersonnes] (a single table) and [dbecole] (four related tables: classes, students, subjects, and grades). This chapter is identical to the first one, then combines the two chapters ORM into a single one: Dart has no mature equivalent of [TypeORM] or [Prisma] for MySQL (see the sidebar at the end of the chapter), and rather than forcing an artificial correspondence with either one, we construct a “lightweight ORM” that demonstrates what a ORM actually does, by writing it ourselves.

docs.title: 7.1. Direct access to the database
docs.text: The TypeScript [mysql2] package has no equivalent maintained by the MySQL team itself on the Dart side. An early version of this chapter used [package:mysql1] (pub.dev/packages/mysql1), a widely used pure Dart driver—MySQL—but it turned out to be incompatible with MySQL 8.4 (the version shipped with Laragon): even a query as simple as “select 1” consistently failed with the protocol error “Got packets out of order,” a known and unresolved bug in the package (issues GitHub adamlofts/mysql1_dart #112 and #161). We are therefore now using [package:mysql_client_plus] (pub.dev/packages/mysql_client_plus), an actively maintained fork that has been tested with MySQL and 8.x, including API — [MySQLConnection.createConnection], [connexion.connect], [connexion.execute], [connexion.close] — remains very similar to that of [mysql2].

docs.title: 7.1.1. Preparing the [dbpersonnes] database
docs.text:
The dbpersonnes database contains only one table, personnes, which uses the same schema as the one used in the Python course (columns id, first\_name, last\_name, age, with a uniqueness constraint on the pair (last\_name, first\_name)). The script sql/create_dbpersonnes.sql below creates the database, the application user, and the table, then inserts five arbitrary people into it:

-- create_dbpersonnes.sql
-- Recrée la base [dbpersonnes] utilisée par le chapitre « Accès à MySQL avec le
-- pilote natif [mysql2] », avec des données arbitraires (les originales du cours
-- Python/Flask 2020 n'étant plus disponibles).
--
-- Utilisation :
-- mysql -u root -p < create_dbpersonnes.sql
--
-- Crée la base, l'utilisateur applicatif [admpersonnes/nobody] (mêmes
-- identifiants que le cours d'origine) et la table [personnes].

DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS dbpersonnes;
CREATE DATABASE dbpersonnes CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;

CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS 'admpersonnes'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'nobody';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON dbpersonnes.* TO 'admpersonnes'@'localhost';
FLUSH PRIVILEGES;

USE dbpersonnes;

CREATE TABLE personnes (
  id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  prenom VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
  nom VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
  age INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (nom, prenom)
);

-- données arbitraires (mêmes personnes que les exemples du cours d'origine)
INSERT INTO personnes (id, prenom, nom, age) VALUES
(1, 'Paul', 'Langevin', 48),
(2, 'Sylvie', 'Lefur', 70),
(3, 'Pierre', 'Nicazou', 35),
(4, 'Geraldine','Colou', 26),
(5, 'Paulette', 'Girond', 56);

To create this database (MySQL), you can use Laragon’s [HeidiSQL] tool. We’ve already used it.

  • In [1], start all Laragon services. This will start SGBD and MySQL;
  • in [2], access the [HeidiSQL] database management tool;
  • In [1-2], log in to MySQL;

Using [1-2], run the two SQL files in the project one after the other:

While still in [HeidiSQL], run F5 to refresh the display:

We are now ready to use these two databases.

docs.title: 7.1.2. [mysql_01] script
docs.text:
// mysql_01.dart
// Database: databases/mysql/mysql-01.ts.
//
// First step: log in to the database MySQL [dbpersonnes], then
// log out.
//
// [choix technique] The TypeScript [mysql2] package has no direct equivalent
// Dart-side direct version maintained by the MySQL team itself. An early
// version of this chapter used [package:mysql1] (pub.dev/packages/
// mysql1), a widely used pure Dart driver—but one that
// proved to be incompatible with MySQL 8.4 (included with Laragon): even a query
// as trivial as "select 1" would consistently fail with the
// protocol error “Got packets out of order” (a known, unresolved bug in the
// packet). Therefore, we use [package:mysql_client_plus]
// (pub.dev/packages/mysql_client_plus), an actively maintained fork, and
// tested with MySQL 8.x, including API - [MySQLConnection.createConnection],
// [connexion.connect], [connexion.execute], [connexion.close] - remains very
// close to that of [mysql2].
import 'package:mysql_client_plus/mysql_client_plus.dart';

// connection to the database MySQL [dbpersonnes]
// the user's identity is (admpersonnes, nobody)
const String user = 'admpersonnes';
const String pwd = 'nobody';
const String host = 'localhost';
const int port = 3306;
const String database = 'dbpersonnes';

Future<void> main() async {
  // [différence avec TypeScript] no union type "MySqlConnection |
  // "undefined" here: a nullable field ([MySQLConnection?]) plays the same
  // role—"not yet logged in" is represented by [null], exactly
  // as “not yet logged in” was represented by [undefined] on the TS side.
  MySQLConnection? connexion;
  try {
    print('Connexion au SGBD MySQL en cours...');
    // [différence avec TypeScript] unlike mysql1 (and mysql2),
    // [mysql_client_plus] separates the CRÉATION from the connection object
    // ([createConnection], which does not yet involve any network traffic) from
    // the actual establishment of the connection ([connect], which negotiates the
    // protocol with the server)—two distinct stages, whereas
    // mysql1 conflated them into a single call [MySqlConnection.connect].
    // [connexion] (the nullable variable from the [finally] block) is not assigned
    // only after [connect] succeeds: if [connect] fails, [connexion]
    // remains [null], and [finally] will not attempt to close a connection
    // that was never actually opened.
    final nouvelleConnexion = await MySQLConnection.createConnection(
      host: host,
      port: port,
      userName: user,
      password: pwd,
      databaseName: database,
    );
    await nouvelleConnexion.connect();
    connexion = nouvelleConnexion;
    // followed by
    print(
      "Connexion MySQL réussie à la base database=$database, host=$host sous l'identité user=$user, passwd=$pwd",
    );
  } catch (erreur) {
    // displays the error
    print("L'erreur suivante s'est produite : $erreur");
  } finally {
    // the connection is closed if it was opened
    if (connexion != null) {
      await connexion.close();
    }
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 19: [import 'package:mysql_client_plus/mysql_client_plus.dart';]: the new MySQL driver written entirely in Dart, replacing [package:mysql1]—which is incompatible with MySQL 8.4 (included with Laragon): even a query as trivial as “select 1” would consistently fail with the protocol error “Got packets out of order,” a known and unresolved bug in the package (see the comment at the top of the file).
  • Line 34: [MySQLConnection? connexion;]: a NULLABLE field serves exactly the same purpose as the union type [MySqlConnection | undefined] of TypeScript - [null] represents “not yet connected,” just like [undefined] relative to TS.
  • Lines 47–55: [final nouvelleConnexion = await MySQLConnection.createConnection(...); await nouvelleConnexion.connect(); connexion = nouvelleConnexion;]: [mysql_client_plus] separates CRÉATION from the connection object ([createConnection], which is not yet exchanging any network traffic) to the actual establishment of the connection ([connect], which negotiates the protocol with the server)—two distinct stages, whereas [mysql1] (like [mysql2] on the TypeScript side) combined them into a single call. [connexion] (the nullable variable from [finally]) is assigned only after [connect] succeeds, so that [finally] never closes a connection that was never actually opened.
  • [try] / [catch] / [finally]: structure identical to the previous version—the connection is always closed in [finally], regardless of whether an error occurred.

The result of the execution is as follows:

Connexion au SGBD MySQL en cours...
Connexion MySQL réussie à la base database=dbpersonnes, host=localhost sous l'identité user=admpersonnes, passwd=nobody

docs.title: 7.1.3. [mysql_02] script
docs.text:
// mysql_02.dart
// Port databases/mysql/mysql-02.ts.
//
// In this new script, the database connection is isolated in a
// function.
import 'package:mysql_client_plus/mysql_client_plus.dart';

// connects to and then disconnects from (login, password) the database [database] on the server
// [hote]; throws an exception if there is a problem
Future<void> connexion(String hote, int port, String database, String login, String pwd) async {
  MySQLConnection? cnx;
  try {
    // connection—[createConnection] creates the object; [connect] actually negotiates
    // actually negotiates with the server (see comment on mysql_01.dart); we
    // only affects [cnx] after a successful [connect], so that [finally]
    // never closes a connection that failed
    final nouvelleConnexion = await MySQLConnection.createConnection(
      host: hote,
      port: port,
      userName: login,
      password: pwd,
      databaseName: database,
    );
    await nouvelleConnexion.connect();
    cnx = nouvelleConnexion;
    print(
      "Connexion réussie à la base database=$database, host=$hote sous l'identité user=$login, passwd=$pwd",
    );
  } finally {
    // the connection is closed if it has been opened
    if (cnx != null) {
      await cnx.close();
      print('Déconnexion réussie\n');
    }
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------- main
// connection credentials
const String user = 'admpersonnes';
const String passwd = 'nobody';
const String host = 'localhost';
const int port = 3306;
const String database = 'dbpersonnes';

Future<void> main() async {
  // Login for an existing user
  try {
    await connexion(host, port, database, user, passwd);
  } catch (erreur) {
    // the error is displayed
    print('$erreur');
  }

  // Login by a nonexistent user
  try {
    await connexion(host, port, database, 'xx', 'xx');
  } catch (erreur) {
    // error displayed
    print('$erreur');
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 10–36: [Future<void> connexion(String hote, int port, String database, String login, String pwd) async { ... }]: The connection is encapsulated in a reusable function, which throws an exception in case of failure rather than catching it itself—it’s up to the caller to decide what to do with it. It reuses the “creation + [connect()]” pattern from [mysql_01.dart]: [cnx] is only assigned after a successful [connect].
  • Line 43: [const int port = 3306;]: [mysql_client_plus] requires a port EXPLICITE ([createConnection]), whereas [ConnectionSettings] derived the default port on its own from [mysql1] (3306).
  • [main] calls this function twice, in two separate blocks, [try] and [catch]: once with valid identifiers and once with invalid identifiers, to illustrate both paths.

The result of the execution is as follows:

Connexion réussie à la base database=dbpersonnes, host=localhost sous l'identité user=admpersonnes, passwd=nobody
Déconnexion réussie

MySQLServerException [1045]: Access denied for user 'xx'@'localhost' (using password: YES)

docs.title: 7.1.4. script [mysql_03]
docs.text:
// mysql_03.dart
// Database: databases/mysql/mysql-03.ts.
//
// Now that we know how to connect, we issue commands SQL on the
// connection: we (re)create the table [personnes] in the database [dbpersonnes].
import 'dart:io';
import 'package:mysql_client_plus/mysql_client_plus.dart';

// executes an update query on the connection
Future<void> executeSql(MySQLConnection connexion, String requete) async {
  await connexion.execute(requete);
}

// ---------------------------------------------- main
// connection credentials
const String id = 'admpersonnes';
const String pwd = 'nobody';
const String host = 'localhost';
const int port = 3306;
const String database = 'dbpersonnes';

Future<void> main() async {
  // Let’s take it step by step
  late final MySQLConnection connexion;
  try {
    // connection - [package:mysql_client_plus], like mysql1 before it,
    // executes each query in its own transaction by default
    // auto-commit (equivalent to AUTOCOMMIT=True on the Python side)
    connexion = await MySQLConnection.createConnection(
      host: host,
      port: port,
      userName: id,
      password: pwd,
      databaseName: database,
    );
    await connexion.connect();
  } catch (erreur) {
    print("L'erreur suivante s'est produite : $erreur");
    // [différence avec TypeScript] `process.exit(1)` becomes `exit(1)`
    // (dart:io) - same semantics, same process exit code
    exit(1);
  }

  // Delete the "people" table if it exists
  // if it does not exist, an error will occur—this is ignored
  try {
    await executeSql(connexion, 'drop table personnes');
  } catch (_) {
    // ignored—[_] indicates that the exception value is ignored
  }

  // Create the "people" table
  const requete = 'create table personnes (id int PRIMARY KEY, prenom varchar(30) NOT NULL, nom varchar(30) NOT NULL, '
      'age integer NOT NULL, unique(nom,prenom))';
  try {
    await executeSql(connexion, requete);
    print('$requete : requête réussie');
  } catch (erreur) {
    print("L'erreur suivante s'est produite : $erreur");
  } finally {
    await connexion.close();
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 10–12: [Future<void> executeSql(MySQLConnection connexion, String requete) async { await connexion.execute(requete); }]: a utility function to execute a SQL update command (here, a DROP TABLE followed by a CREATE TABLE) - [connexion.execute(...)] replaces [connexion.query(...)] from [mysql1] (same role, new method name on the [mysql_client_plus] side).
  • Line 41: [exit(1);] (from [dart:io]): equivalent to [process.exit(1)]—same semantics, same process exit code in the event of a connection failure.
  • Line 47: [try { await executeSql(connexion, 'drop table personnes'); } catch (_) {}]: The fact that [_] is passed as a parameter to [catch] indicates that the exception value is being ignored—the table may simply not exist yet.

The result of the execution is as follows:

create table personnes (id int PRIMARY KEY, prenom varchar(30) NOT NULL, nom varchar(30) NOT NULL, age integer NOT NULL, unique(nom,prenom)) : requête réussie

docs.title: 7.1.5. script [config_04]
docs.text:
// config_04.dart
// Database: databases/mysql/config-04.ts.
//
// Configuring the [mysql_04] script: path to the SQL command file
// and database connection credentials [dbpersonnes].
//
// [différence avec TypeScript] config-04.ts locates the script folder
// using `dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`. Dart has a
// direct and shorter equivalent: [Platform.script] (dart:io) is already
// the URI of the currently running script—you just need to resolve a relative path
// relative to [.resolve(...)], without any string manipulation. Note:
// [Platform.script] refers to the script PRINCIPAL launched by `dart run`
// (mysql_04.dart), not this file—unlike `import.meta.url`,
// is unique to each file. The result is identical here since
//, config_04.dart, and mysql_04.dart are located in the same folder.
import 'dart:io';

class Config {
  final String commandsFilename;
  final String host;
  // [migration mysql_client_plus] unlike mysql1, whose
  // [ConnectionSettings] deduced the default port (3306) on its own,
  // [MySQLConnection.createConnection] requires a port EXPLICITE—so
  // so we’re adding it here to the configuration.
  final int port;
  final String database;
  final String user;
  final String password;

  const Config({
    required this.commandsFilename,
    required this.host,
    required this.port,
    required this.database,
    required this.user,
    required this.password,
  });
}

Config configure() {
  return Config(
    // command file SQL, resolved relative to CE file
    commandsFilename: Platform.script.resolve('data/commandes.sql').toFilePath(),
    // database connection credentials
    host: 'localhost',
    port: 3306,
    database: 'dbpersonnes',
    user: 'admpersonnes',
    password: 'nobody',
  );
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 43: [Platform.script.resolve('data/commandes.sql').toFilePath()] (from [dart:io]): the direct and shorter equivalent of [dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))] relative to TypeScript - [Platform.script] is already the URI of the currently running script; all that’s needed is to resolve a relative path within it.
  • Important note: [Platform.script] refers to the script PRINCIPAL launched by [dart run] (in this case, [mysql_04.dart]), not necessarily the file where the expression is written—unlike [import.meta.url], which is unique to each file. The result is still correct here since [config_04.dart] and [mysql_04.dart] reside in the same folder.
  • lines 18–28: [class Config { final String commandsFilename; ...; final int port; ...; const Config({required this... }); }]: an immutable class to group the configuration, like the [Config] interface of version TypeScript — with an additional [port] field, explicitly required by [MySQLConnection.createConnection] (whereas [ConnectionSettings] from [mysql1] automatically inferred the default port, 3306).

docs.title: 7.1.6. script [mysql_module]
docs.text:
// mysql_module.dart
// databases/mysql/mysql-module.ts directory: reusable functions for
// executing a list (or file) of SQL commands on an open connection
// MySQL.
//
// [migration] This file originally used [package:mysql1], which was
// proved to be incompatible with MySQL 8.4 (see comment by pubspec.yaml). It was
// been ported to [package:mysql_client_plus]—see below for the difference
// that this changes how transactions are handled.
import 'dart:io';
import 'package:mysql_client_plus/mysql_client_plus.dart';

// displays the result of a SQL command (result of an execute() of
// mysql_client_plus)
// - if [resultats.cols] is not empty, it was a SELECT: display the
// columns and then the rows;
// - otherwise, it was an update command (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL):
// displays the number of modified rows ([resultats.affectedRows],
// equivalent to the [rowcount] for a cursor).
void _afficherInfos(IResultSet resultats) {
  if (resultats.cols.isNotEmpty) {
    // this was a SELECT - [cols] describes the requested columns
    final titres = resultats.cols.map((c) => c.name).toList();
    final entete = titres.join(', ');
    print(entete);
    print('*' * entete.length);
    for (final ligne in resultats.rows) {
      print(titres.map((t) => ligne.colByName(t)).toList());
    }
    print('*' * entete.length);
  } else {
    // no columns described—update order
    print('nombre de lignes modifiées : ${resultats.affectedRows}');
  }
}

// uses the open connection [connexion]
// executes the SQL commands contained in the list on this connection
// [commandesSql] (one command per element; empty lines or
// lines starting with # are ignored)
// - if follow=true, each execution of a SQL command is followed by a
// message indicating whether it succeeded or failed;
// - if stop=true, the function stops at the first error encountered,
// otherwise, it executes all commands;
// - if avecTransaction=true, any error cancels all previously executed SQL
// that were previously executed (rollback); otherwise, each command is validated
// independently (default behavior of MySQL, in AUTOCOMMIT);
// the function returns a list [erreur1, erreur2, ...]
//
// [différence avec TypeScript] mysql2 exposes directly
// `connexion.beginTransaction()/commit()/rollback()`. [package:mysql1]
// (used in an earlier version of this file) did not expose these
// methods one by one: the transaction had to be controlled “manually” by
// sending the commands SQL, [START TRANSACTION], [COMMIT], and
// [ROLLBACK]. [package:mysql_client_plus] finally provides the direct equivalent
// of mysql2: `connexion.transactional<T>((cnx) async { ... })` executes the
// callback within a transaction, automatically commits (COMMIT) if it
// completes normally, and automatically rolls back (ROLLBACK) if it throws a
// exception—no further SQL transaction control commands to write
// ourselves.
Future<List<String>> executeListOfCommands(
  MySQLConnection connexion,
  List<String> commandesSql, {
  bool suivi = false,
  bool arret = true,
  bool avecTransaction = true,
}) async {
  final erreurs = <String>[];

  //actually executes the commands on the provided connection [cnx]: this is
  // either [connexion] itself (no transaction) or the
  // "working" connection that [transactional] provides to its callback (with
  // transaction)—the loop is written only once for both cases
  Future<void> executerCommandes(MySQLConnection cnx) async {
    for (final commandeBrute in commandesSql) {
      // we remove the leading and trailing whitespace from the current command
      final commande = commandeBrute.trim();
      // Is the command empty or a comment? Move on to the next one
      if (commande == '' || commande[0] == '#') {
        continue;
      }
      // execute the current command
      try {
        final resultats = await cnx.execute(commande);
        // No error
        if (suivi) {
          print('[$commande] : Exécution réussie');
        }
        _afficherInfos(resultats);
      } catch (erreur) {
        final msg = '$commande : Erreur ($erreur)';
        erreurs.add(msg);
        if (suivi) {
          print(msg);
        }
        // Stop?
        if (avecTransaction || arret) {
          // With transaction: Re-trigger the error so that
          // [connexion.transactional] triggers ROLLBACK - with
          // [package:mysql_client_plus], it is EXCEPTION that controls
          // the cancellation, not just a loop termination as with the
          // ROLLBACK manual for the mysql1 version
          if (avecTransaction) rethrow;
          return;
        }
      }
    }
  }

  if (avecTransaction) {
    try {
      await connexion.transactional((cnx) => executerCommandes(cnx));
    } catch (_) {
      // the error has already been logged in [erreurs] above; it
      // suppress it here to return the list of errors normally to
      // the caller, exactly as the mysql1 version did (which
      // never allowed exceptions to escape from this function)
    }
  } else {
    await executerCommandes(connexion);
  }
  return erreurs;
}

// uses the open connection [connexion]
// executes the commands SQL contained in the file
// text file [sqlFilename] (one command per line)
Future<List<String>> executeFileOfCommands(
  MySQLConnection connexion,
  String sqlFilename, {
  bool suivi = false,
  bool arret = true,
  bool avecTransaction = true,
}) async {
  try {
    final contenu = await File(sqlFilename).readAsString();
    return await executeListOfCommands(
      connexion,
      contenu.split('\n'),
      suivi: suivi,
      arret: arret,
      avecTransaction: avecTransaction,
    );
  } catch (erreur) {
    return ["Le fichier $sqlFilename n'a pu être exploité : $erreur"];
  }
}

Let's comment on this code:

  • line 20: [void _afficherInfos(IResultSet resultats)]: distinguishes a SELECT ([resultats.cols] describes the requested columns) from an update statement ([resultats.affectedRows], equivalent to the [rowcount] for a cursor) - [resultats.cols]/[resultats.rows] replace [resultats.fields] from [mysql1], and [ligne.colByName(t)] replaces the [ligne.fields[t]] entry.
  • Lines 61–67: [Future<List<String>> executeListOfCommands(MySQLConnection connexion, List<String> commandesSql, {bool suivi = false, bool arret = true, bool avecTransaction = true}) async { ... }]: PARAMÈTRES and NOMMÉS with default values, unchanged since version [mysql1]—exactly like the optional parameters of the TypeScript configuration object.
  • Lines 74–108: [Future<void> executerCommandes(MySQLConnection cnx) async { ... }]: a (nested) LOCALE function, reused for both the “with transaction” case (in which it receives the working connection that [transactional] provides to its callback) and the “without transaction” case (in which case it receives [connexion] directly)—thus, the command execution loop is written only once. With a transaction, it is a re-launched EXCEPTION ([rethrow]) that triggers the ROLLBACK, rather than a simple loop termination as with the manual ROLLBACK in version [mysql1].
  • Lines 110–118: [if (avecTransaction) { try { await connexion.transactional((cnx) => executerCommandes(cnx)); } catch (_) { ... } }]: [mysql2] directly exposes [connexion.beginTransaction()]/[commit()]/[rollback()]. [package:mysql1] did not expose these methods one by one: you had to control the transaction “manually” by sending the commands SQL, [START TRANSACTION], [COMMIT], and [ROLLBACK] yourself. [package:mysql_client_plus] finally provides the direct equivalent of [mysql2]: [connexion.transactional((cnx) async { ... })] executes the callback within a transaction, automatically commits (COMMIT) if it completes normally, and automatically rolls back (ROLLBACK) if it throws an exception—no more need to write your own SQL transaction control statements.
  • Lines 128–134: [Future<List<String>> executeFileOfCommands(...) async { ... }]: reads a file ([File(sqlFilename).readAsString()]) and then delegates to [executeListOfCommands]—unchanged since version [mysql1], same structure as in TypeScript.

docs.title: 7.1.7. script [mysql_04]
docs.text:
This main script coordinates the two previous scripts to execute the file [data/commandes.sql] (identical to the TypeScript course), with or without a transaction depending on the command-line argument provided.

// mysql_04.dart
// Directory databases/mysql/mysql-04.ts.
//
// Main script: runs the SQL command file
// [data/commandes.sql], with or without a transaction depending on the argument passed
// on the command line.
// dart run mysql_04.dart true (with transaction)
// dart run mysql_04.dart false (without transaction)
import 'dart:io';
import 'package:mysql_client_plus/mysql_client_plus.dart';
import 'config_04.dart';
import 'mysql_module.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> arguments) async {
  final config = configure();

  // ---------------------------------------------- main
  // checking the syntax of the call
  bool erreur = arguments.length != 1;
  String avecTransactionTexte = '';
  if (!erreur) {
    avecTransactionTexte = arguments[0].toLowerCase();
    erreur = avecTransactionTexte != 'true' && avecTransactionTexte != 'false';
  }
  if (erreur) {
    print('syntaxe : dart run mysql_04.dart true / false');
    exit(1);
  }

  // text calculation
  final avecTransaction = avecTransactionTexte == 'true';
  final texte = avecTransaction ? 'avec transaction' : 'sans transaction';

  // screen logs
  print('--------------------------------------------------------------------');
  print('Exécution du fichier SQL ${config.commandsFilename} $texte');
  print('--------------------------------------------------------------------');

  // Execution of commands SQL from the file
  MySQLConnection? connexion;
  List<String> erreurs = [];
  try {
    // Connection to the database—[connexion] is assigned only once to [connect]
    // successful (see comment on mysql_01.dart)
    final nouvelleConnexion = await MySQLConnection.createConnection(
      host: config.host,
      port: config.port,
      userName: config.user,
      password: config.password,
      databaseName: config.database,
    );
    await nouvelleConnexion.connect();
    connexion = nouvelleConnexion;
    // executing the SQL command file
    erreurs = await executeFileOfCommands(
      connexion,
      config.commandsFilename,
      suivi: true,
      arret: false,
      avecTransaction: avecTransaction,
    );
  } catch (erreurFatale) {
    print("L'erreur fatale suivante s'est produite : $erreurFatale");
    exit(1);
  } finally {
    if (connexion != null) {
      await connexion.close();
    }
  }

  // displaying the number of errors
  print('--------------------------------------------------------------------');
  print('Exécution terminée');
  print('--------------------------------------------------------------------');
  print('Il y a eu ${erreurs.length} erreur(s)');
  for (final erreurCourante in erreurs) {
    print(erreurCourante);
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 14–28: [Future<void> main(List<String> arguments) async { ... }]: [arguments] receives parameters from the command line, just like [process.argv.slice(2)] on the Node side—here, a single argument is expected: [true] or [false].
  • Lines 45–53: [final nouvelleConnexion = await MySQLConnection.createConnection(...); await nouvelleConnexion.connect(); connexion = nouvelleConnexion;]: The connection uses the same creation pattern as [connect()], as shown in [mysql_01.dart], with parameters taken from [config] (including the new field [port]).
  • Lines 55–61: [executeFileOfCommands(connexion, config.commandsFilename, suivi: true, arret: false, avecTransaction: avecTransaction)]: Executes [data/commandes.sql], with or without a transaction depending on the argument—[dart run mysql_04.dart true] or [dart run mysql_04.dart false].

docs.title: 7.1.8. script [mysql_05]
docs.text:
// mysql_05.dart
// Database: databases/mysql/mysql-05.ts.
//
// Parameterized queries: prepared single insertion, followed by insertion in
// table. Here, we recreate the table [personnes] with the column schema [id]
// (as in the script mysql_03), so that this script is independent of
// the state left by mysql_04.
import 'package:mysql_client_plus/mysql_client_plus.dart';

// the user's identity
const String id = 'admpersonnes';
const String pwd = 'nobody';
// the DBMS host machine
const String host = 'localhost';
const int port = 3306;
// the database name
const String base = 'dbpersonnes';

// [différence avec TypeScript] `type Person = [id: number, last_name: string,
// first_name: string, age: number]` (a tuple TypeScript, which is named but remains
// a simple array at runtime) becomes a RECORD POSITIONNEL Dart
// 3 (see dart-fundamentals/dart3/dart3_01_records.dart): the same concept of a
// "small group of typed values, with no class to write," but a true
// type in its own right, distinct from a [List].
typedef Personne = (int id, String nom, String prenom, int age);

Future<void> main() async {
  // list of people (id, last name, first name, age)
  final personnes = <Personne>[
    for (var i = 0; i < 5; i++) (i, 'n0$i', 'p0$i', i + 10),
    (40, "d'Aboot", "Y'éna", 18),
  ];

  // another list of people
  final autresPersonnes = <Personne>[
    for (var i = 0; i < 5; i++) (i + 100, 'n1$i', 'p1$i', i + 20),
    (200, "d'Aboot", "F'ilhem", 34),
  ];

  // access to SGBD
  MySQLConnection? connexion;
  try {
    // Login—[connexion] is assigned only after [connect] is successful
    // (see comment on mysql_01.dart)
    final nouvelleConnexion = await MySQLConnection.createConnection(
      host: host,
      port: port,
      userName: id,
      password: pwd,
      databaseName: base,
    );
    await nouvelleConnexion.connect();
    connexion = nouvelleConnexion;

    // (re)creation of the table with the column-oriented schema [id] (see mysql_03)
    await connexion.execute('drop table if exists personnes');
    await connexion.execute(
      'create table people (id int PRIMARY KEY, first_name varchar(30) NOT NULL, last_name varchar(30) NOT NULL, '
      'age integer NOT NULL, unique(nom,prenom))',
    );

    // deleting existing records
    await connexion.execute('delete from personnes');
    // insertions one person at a time using a parameterized query -
    // deserializing the positional record [personne] directly into
    // the for loop header (see dart-fundamentals/dart3/dart3_02_patterns.dart)
    //
    // [différence avec TypeScript et avec mysql1] mysql2 (and mysql1, in
    // an earlier version of this script) use PLACEHOLDERS
    // POSITIONNELS ("?", associated with a LISTE of values in the same
    // order). [package:mysql_client_plus] works differently: the
    // placeholders are NOMMÉS (":id", ":name"...) and associated with a [Map]
    // (placeholder name -> value)—more verbose to write here, but
    // makes each request independent of the ORDRE parameters.
    for (final (idP, nom, prenom, age) in personnes) {
      await connexion.execute(
        'insert into personnes(id,nom,prenom,age) values(:id,:nom,:prenom,:age)',
        {'id': idP, 'nom': nom, 'prenom': prenom, 'age': age},
      );
    }
    // [différence avec TypeScript] mysql2 offers
    // `connexion.query('insert ... values ?', [[[...],[...],...]])`, which
    // automatically constructs a single multi-row query from a
    // array of arrays. [package:mysql_client_plus] does not have this
    // equivalent (like mysql1 before it): so you have to construct the
    // text SQL, with a group of placeholders NOMMÉS per line (":id0",
    // ":name0"... ":id1", ":name1"...) since named placeholders
    // cannot be repeated in the same request—a single round trip
    // network round trip, like the version TypeScript.
    final groupePlaceholders = <String>[];
    final valeurs = <String, Object?>{};
    for (var i = 0; i < autresPersonnes.length; i++) {
      final (idP, nom, prenom, age) = autresPersonnes[i];
      groupePlaceholders.add('(:id$i,:nom$i,:prenom$i,:age$i)');
      valeurs['id$i'] = idP;
      valeurs['nom$i'] = nom;
      valeurs['prenom$i'] = prenom;
      valeurs['age$i'] = age;
    }
    await connexion.execute(
      'insert into personnes(id,nom,prenom,age) values ${groupePlaceholders.join(',')}',
      valeurs,
    );

    // transaction validation—here, each request has already been
    // self-validated (MySQL is set to AUTOCOMMIT by default, as the mode
    // default mode mentioned in the script mysql_03); therefore, there is nothing to validate
    // explicitly
    print('${personnes.length + autresPersonnes.length} personnes insérées.');
  } catch (erreur) {
    print("L'erreur suivante s'est produite : $erreur");
  } finally {
    if (connexion != null) {
      await connexion.close();
    }
  }
}

Let's comment on this code:

  • line 25: [typedef Personne = (int id, String nom, String prenom, int age);]: the tuple TypeScript, named [type Personne = [id: number, nom: string, prenom: string, age: number]] (a simple array at runtime) becomes a RECORD POSITIONNEL in Dart 3—a fully-fledged type in its own right, distinct from a [List].
  • Lines 75–80: [for (final (idP, nom, prenom, age) in personnes) { await connexion.execute('insert into personnes(id,nom,prenom,age) values(:id,:nom,:prenom,:age)', {'id': idP, 'nom': nom, 'prenom': prenom, 'age': age}); }]: each prepared insertion directly deconstructs the positional record in the [for] header (see the chapter “What’s New in Dart” 3.x)—with placeholders NOMMÉS ([:id], [:nom]...) associated with a [Map], instead of the POSITIONNELS ([?] + list of values) for [mysql1] and [mysql2].
  • Lines 90–99: [final groupePlaceholders = <String>[]; final valeurs = <String, Object?>{}; for (...) { groupePlaceholders.add('(:id$i,:nom$i,:prenom$i,:age$i)'); ... }]: [mysql2] directly supports bulk insertion from an array of arrays ([values ?] with [[[...],[...]]]). [package:mysql_client_plus] does not have this equivalent (like [mysql1] before it): so you must construct the text for SQL yourself, but with a group of placeholders—NOMMÉS and NUMÉROTÉS—per line ([:id0], [:nom0]... [:id1], [:nom1]...), since named placeholders cannot be repeated within the same request—a single network round trip, like the TypeScript version.
  • Line 93: [final (idP, nom, prenom, age) = autresPersonnes[i];]: again, a positional record decomposition—necessary here to individually name each placeholder ([:id0], [:nom0]...) based on the record’s four fields, since [mysql_client_plus] does not provide direct positional access like [p.$1, p.$2...], which was used in the previous version of this script.

The result of the execution is as follows:

12 personnes insérées.

docs.title: 7.1.9. Conclusion
docs.text: The port of the native driver is faithful to the original TypeScript. After an initial attempt with [package:mysql1]—which was abandoned due to incompatibility with MySQL 8.4— [package:mysql_client_plus] ultimately provides a API that is even closer to [mysql2] than [mysql1] was: [connexion.transactional(...)] is the direct equivalent of [beginTransaction()]/[commit()]/[rollback()], whereas [mysql1] would have required manually managing the transaction using the commands SQL, [START TRANSACTION], [COMMIT], and [ROLLBACK]. One difference remains, albeit a more subtle one: the columns DECIMAL ([matieres.coefficient], [notes.valeur] in the [dbecole] database) require an explicit conversion using a small helper [_decimal] ([typedColByName<String>(...)] then [num.parse(...)]), since direct conversion to [num] or [double] is not supported by the driver for this SQL type.

docs.title: 7.2. The lightweight ORM
docs.text:
The TypeScript course devotes two separate chapters to accessing databases via a ORM ([Object-Relational Mapping]): [TypeORM], followed by [Prisma], using the same example schema. Both are based on a common principle: describe the schema once (using TypeORM decorators on classes, or a [.prisma] file for Prisma), then letting the tool generate, at startup or during compilation, all the code that translates object reads/writes into SQL—including the loading of relationships between tables.

Dart does not have a mature and widely adopted equivalent to these two tools for MySQL: there are Dart ORM libraries, but they are primarily designed for Flutter/SQLite ([Drift], [Floor]) or for different architectures - Prisma itself does not offer a Dart client. Rather than forcing an artificial mapping such as “such-and-such Dart package = TypeORM” or “such-and-such package = Prisma,” this chapter takes a different approach, one that is more educationally sound: showing what a ORM actually does by writing it yourself in a deliberately minimal version—hence the name [ORM léger].

docs.title: 7.2.1. The entities: the [entities.dart] file
docs.text:
// entities.dart
// Contains the entities TypeORM (databases/typeorm/entities/*.entity.ts):
// Person (database [dbpersonnes]), and Class / Student / Subject / Grade (database
// [dbecole]).
//
// [différence de fond avec TypeScript] The entities TypeORM are
// ordinary classes DÉCORÉES (`@Entity`, `@Column`, `@ManyToOne`...):
// it is TypeORM, at startup, that LIT these decorators (a form of
// reflection/metaprogramming) to determine how to read/write each
// field in SQL, and how to load a relationship on demand. Dart has
// no equivalent of reflection that can be used here (`dart:mirrors` has been
// deprecated for web compilation/AOT): these classes are therefore simply
// simply mutable “bags of fields,” without any annotations—this is the
// entire orm_leger package (repository.dart in particular) that,
// handwritten, plays the role that reflection plays for TypeORM. See
// the README.md in this thread for the full discussion.
class Personne {
  int id;
  String nom;
  String prenom;
  int age;

  Personne({required this.id, required this.nom, required this.prenom, required this.age});

  @override
  String toString() => 'Personne($id, $prenom $nom, $age ans)';
}

class Classe {
  int id;
  String nom;
  // reverse relationship (backref from Eleve.classe) - PAS loaded
  // automatically: remains empty until a query is explicitly called
  // a query that populates it (see orm_03_joined_queries.dart)
  List<Eleve> eleves = [];

  Classe({required this.id, required this.nom});

  @override
  String toString() => 'Classe($id, $nom)';
}

class Eleve {
  int id;
  String nom;
  String prenom;
  int classeId;
  // N-1 relationship to Class—null until it has been loaded
  // explicitly (equivalent to the option `relations: { class: true }`
  // from TypeORM, but rendered here as a regular nullable field)
  Classe? classe;
  List<Note> notes = [];

  Eleve({
    required this.id,
    required this.nom,
    required this.prenom,
    required this.classeId,
    this.classe,
  });

  @override
  String toString() => 'Eleve($id, $prenom $nom)';
}

class Matiere {
  int id;
  String nom;
  num coefficient;
  List<Note> notes = [];

  Matiere({required this.id, required this.nom, required this.coefficient});

  @override
  String toString() => 'Matiere($id, $nom, coefficient $coefficient)';
}

class Note {
  int id;
  num valeur;
  int eleveId;
  int matiereId;
  Eleve? eleve;
  Matiere? matiere;

  Note({
    required this.id,
    required this.valeur,
    required this.eleveId,
    required this.matiereId,
    this.eleve,
    this.matiere,
  });

  @override
  String toString() => 'Note($id, $valeur)';
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • The TypeORM entities are ordinary DÉCORÉES classes ([@Entity], [@Column], [@ManyToOne]...): It is TypeORM that, at startup, reads these decorators (a form of reflection) to determine how to read/write each field in SQL, and to load a relationship on demand. Dart has no equivalent of reflection that can be used here ([dart:mirrors] is deprecated for web compilation/AOT): these classes are therefore simply mutable “bags of fields,” without any annotations.
  • line 29: [class Classe { ...; List<Eleve> eleves = []; }], [class Eleve { ...; Classe? classe; List<Note> notes = []; }] (line 43): the relationships are simple fields (empty collection or nullable reference) that are never loaded automatically—it is [repository.dart], written by hand, that plays the role that reflection plays for TypeORM.

docs.title: 7.2.2. The generic repository: the [repository.dart] file
docs.text:
// repository.dart
// A hand-written “lightweight ORM”: a very generic [Repository] class
// inspired by the TypeORM Repository (`AppDataSource.getRepository(...)`,
// `.find()`, `.findOneBy()`, `.save()`, `.delete()`), but built on
// a simple table, without decorators or automatic loading of
// relationships—see README.md for a full discussion of this choice.
//
// [migration] This file originally used [package:mysql1]; it was
// ported to [package:mysql_client_plus] (see comment by
// pubspec.yaml). The most noticeable change for the caller is the
// style of parameterized queries: mysql1 used placeholders
// POSITIONNELS ("?" followed by a list of values in order), whereas
// [mysql_client_plus] uses placeholders NOMMÉS (":column" + a
// [Map] column name -> value)—which works out rather well here
// since this repository already works with [Map<String, Object?>] de
// columns.
import 'package:mysql_client_plus/mysql_client_plus.dart';

// [T]: the type of the entity managed by this repository (Person, Class...)
class Repository<T> {
  final MySQLConnection connexion;
  // table name SQL
  final String table;
  // primary key column name
  final String colonneCle;
  // constructs a [T] entity from a SQL result row
  final T Function(ResultSetRow ligne) depuisLigne;
  // returns the columns SQL (column name -> value) of an entity [T],
  // primary key COMPRISE (useful for both insertion and
  // updates)
  final Map<String, Object?> Function(T entite) versColonnes;
  // retrieves the value of the primary key of an entity [T]
  final Object? Function(T entite) cle;

  Repository(
    this.connexion, {
    required this.table,
    required this.colonneCle,
    required this.depuisLigne,
    required this.versColonnes,
    required this.cle,
  });

  // equivalent to `repo.find({ order: { column: 'ASC' } })`
  Future<List<T>> findAll({String? orderBy}) async {
    final sql = 'select * from $table${orderBy != null ? ' order by $orderBy' : ''}';
    final resultats = await connexion.execute(sql);
    return resultats.rows.map(depuisLigne).toList();
  }

  // equivalent to `repo.findOneBy({ column: value })` - [conditions] is
  // an equality "ET" on each provided column; the keys of [conditions]
  // serve as both the column name SQL and the placeholder name
  // NOMMÉ (":column")—they are therefore reused as-is as
  // query parameters
  Future<T?> findOneBy(Map<String, Object?> conditions) async {
    final ou = conditions.keys.map((c) => '$c = :$c').join(' and ');
    final resultats = await connexion.execute(
      'select * from $table where $ou limit 1',
      conditions,
    );
    if (resultats.rows.isEmpty) return null;
    return depuisLigne(resultats.rows.first);
  }

  // equivalent to `repo.findOneByOrFail(...)` / `findOneOrFail(...)`
  Future<T> findOneByOrFail(Map<String, Object?> conditions) async {
    final trouve = await findOneBy(conditions);
    if (trouve == null) {
      throw StateError('Aucune ligne trouvée dans [$table] pour $conditions');
    }
    return trouve;
  }

  // equivalent to `repo.save(entity)`: insert if the key does not exist
  // again, update otherwise—exactly the "upsert" behavior of
  // `save()` on the TypeORM side
  Future<void> save(T entite) async {
    final colonnes = versColonnes(entite);
    final cleCourante = cle(entite);
    final existeDeja = await findOneBy({colonneCle: cleCourante}) != null;
    if (existeDeja) {
      final aMettreAJour = colonnes.keys.where((c) => c != colonneCle);
      final assignations = aMettreAJour.map((c) => '$c = :$c').join(', ');
      // the columns to update, PLUS the key (under the same name as
      // placeholder as in the WHERE clause) — no collision possible
      // since [colonneCle] has just been excluded from [aMettreAJour]
      final valeurs = <String, Object?>{
        for (final c in aMettreAJour) c: colonnes[c],
        colonneCle: cleCourante,
      };
      await connexion.execute('update $table set $assignations where $colonneCle = :$colonneCle', valeurs);
    } else {
      final noms = colonnes.keys.join(',');
      final placeholders = colonnes.keys.map((c) => ':$c').join(',');
      await connexion.execute('insert into $table ($noms) values ($placeholders)', colonnes);
    }
  }

  // equivalent to `repo.delete({ column: value })`
  Future<void> delete(Map<String, Object?> conditions) async {
    final ou = conditions.keys.map((c) => '$c = :$c').join(' and ');
    await connexion.execute('delete from $table where $ou', conditions);
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 20–33: [class Repository<T> { ...; final T Function(ResultSetRow ligne) depuisLigne; final Map<String, Object?> Function(T entite) versColonnes; final Object? Function(T entite) cle; ... }]: a GÉNÉRIQUE class, configured by the [T] entity type, built around TROIS and FONCTIONS provided by the caller—how to read a SQL row, how to write it, and what its primary key is. That is the entirety of “object-relational mapping,” stripped down to the essentials; only the type of the first function has changed since version [mysql1] ([ResultSetRow] instead of [ResultRow]).
  • Line 57: [final ou = conditions.keys.map((c) => '$c = :$c').join(' and ');]: The keys from [conditions] serve as both the column name for SQL and the name for PLACEHOLDER and NOMMÉ ([:colonne]) - unlike [mysql1], which used placeholders POSITIONNELS ([?] plus a LISTE of values in order), [mysql_client_plus] expects a [Map] (placeholder name → value), which works out rather well since this repository already handles [Map<String, Object?>] for columns.
  • Lines 45–63: [Future<List<T>> findAll({String? orderBy}) async { ... }], [Future<T?> findOneBy(Map<String, Object?> conditions) async { ... }]: the direct equivalents of [repo.find(...)] and [repo.findOneBy(...)] for TypeORM - [execute()] replaces [query()], and [resultats.rows] contains the result rows (instead of the list returned directly by [mysql1]).
  • Lines 78–96: [Future<void> save(T entite) async { ...; final existeDeja = await findOneBy(...) != null; if (existeDeja) { ... update ... } else { ... insert ... } }]: the “upsert” behavior of [repo.save(...)]—insert if the key does not yet exist, update otherwise—remains unchanged since version [mysql1], except for the style of the placeholders.

// orm_01_personnes.dart
// Database: databases/typeorm/typeorm-01.ts.
//
// First use of the "lightweight ORM": open the connection, then read
// and write to the table [personnes] via [Repository<Personne>],
// without writing a single line of SQL to the CE file (all of SQL is
// in repository.dart, written once for all entities).
import 'package:mysql_client_plus/mysql_client_plus.dart';
import 'entities.dart';
import 'repository.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  final connexion = await MySQLConnection.createConnection(
    host: 'localhost',
    port: 3306,
    userName: 'admpersonnes',
    password: 'nobody',
    databaseName: 'dbpersonnes',
  );
  await connexion.connect();
  print('Connexion à [dbpersonnes] établie.');

  try {
    final repo = Repository<Personne>(
      connexion,
      table: 'personnes',
      colonneCle: 'id',
      // [migration mysql_client_plus] mysql1 was already decoding each column
      // into the expected native Dart type ([ligne.fields['id'] as int]
      // worked right away). [package:mysql_client_plus] requires an
      // explicit column-by-column access—TYPÉ—which
      // handles the conversion itself; the [!] is safe here since
      // these columns are NOT and NULL in the schema SQL.
      depuisLigne: (ligne) => Personne(
        id: ligne.typedColByName<int>('id')!,
        nom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('nom')!,
        prenom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('prenom')!,
        age: ligne.typedColByName<int>('age')!,
      ),
      versColonnes: (p) => {'id': p.id, 'nom': p.nom, 'prenom': p.prenom, 'age': p.age},
      cle: (p) => p.id,
    );

    // all people, sorted by name
    final toutes = await repo.findAll(orderBy: 'nom asc');
    print('Personnes en base :');
    for (final p in toutes) {
      print('  ${p.id} ${p.prenom} ${p.nom} (${p.age} ans)');
    }

    // a person by its primary key
    final paul = await repo.findOneBy({'id': 1});
    print('Personne id=1 : ${paul != null ? '${paul.prenom} ${paul.nom}' : 'introuvable'}');

    // Insertion of a new person (the entity is a simple class:
    // the constructor is sufficient; no special factory is needed)
    final nouvelle = Personne(id: 99, prenom: 'Ada', nom: 'Lovelace', age: 36);
    await repo.save(nouvelle);
    print('Personne 99 insérée.');

    // update
    nouvelle.age = 37;
    await repo.save(nouvelle);
    print('Après mise à jour, âge=${(await repo.findOneBy({'id': 99}))?.age}');

    // deletion—we restore the database to the state in which we found it
    await repo.delete({'id': 99});
    print('Personne 99 supprimée.');
  } finally {
    await connexion.close();
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 24–42: [final repo = Repository<Personne>(connexion, table: 'personnes', colonneCle: 'id', depuisLigne: (ligne) => Personne(...), versColonnes: (p) => {...}, cle: (p) => p.id);]: builds a repository for the [Personne] entity, providing it with the three expected functions—the only place in the file that “knows” the details of the SQL columns. [mysql1] already decoded each column into the expected native Dart type ([ligne.fields['id'] as int] worked directly); [mysql_client_plus] requests explicit column-by-column access to TYPÉ—[typedColByName<T>(nom)]—which handles the conversion itself.
  • The rest of the script ([repo.findAll], [repo.findOneBy], [repo.save], [repo.delete]) no longer contains any lines from SQL—exactly the same experience provided by TypeORM on a daily basis, unchanged by the migration.

The result of the execution is as follows:

Connexion à [dbpersonnes] établie.
Personnes en base :
40 Y'éna d'Aboot (18 ans)
200 F'ilhem d'Aboot (34 ans)
0 p00 n00 (10 ans)
1 p01 n01 (11 ans)
2 p02 n02 (12 ans)
3 p03 n03 (13 ans)
4 p04 n04 (14 ans)
100 p10 n10 (20 ans)
101 p11 n11 (21 ans)
102 p12 n12 (22 ans)
103 p13 n13 (23 ans)
104 p14 n14 (24 ans)
Personne id=1 : p01 n01
Personne 99 insérée.
Après mise à jour, âge=37
Personne 99 supprimée.

docs.text:
// orm_02_ecole.dart
// Database: databases/typeorm/typeorm-02.ts.
//
// Mapping of three entities from the database [dbecole] (Class, Student, Subject)
// and basic operations (CRUD) through their repositories.
import 'package:mysql_client_plus/mysql_client_plus.dart';
import 'entities.dart';
import 'repository.dart';

// reads a column SQL DECIMAL/NUMERIC (here [matieres.coefficient]) as a
// [num]. [package:mysql_client_plus] can convert a DECIMAL to
// [String] (any SQL can be read as [String]), but PAS
// directly to [num] or [double]—`typedColByName<num>(...)` raises
// then "Cannot convert MySQL type 246 to requested type num" (246 =
// NEWDECIMAL, the internal type MySQL of the columns DECIMAL). We therefore read the
// column as [String], and then convert it ourselves.
num _decimal(ResultSetRow ligne, String colonne) => num.parse(ligne.typedColByName<String>(colonne)!);

Repository<Classe> _repoClasse(MySQLConnection cnx) => Repository<Classe>(
      cnx,
      table: 'classes',
      colonneCle: 'id',
      depuisLigne: (l) => Classe(
        id: l.typedColByName<int>('id')!,
        nom: l.typedColByName<String>('nom')!,
      ),
      versColonnes: (c) => {'id': c.id, 'nom': c.nom},
      cle: (c) => c.id,
    );

Repository<Eleve> _repoEleve(MySQLConnection cnx) => Repository<Eleve>(
      cnx,
      table: 'eleves',
      colonneCle: 'id',
      depuisLigne: (l) => Eleve(
        id: l.typedColByName<int>('id')!,
        nom: l.typedColByName<String>('nom')!,
        prenom: l.typedColByName<String>('prenom')!,
        classeId: l.typedColByName<int>('classe_id')!,
      ),
      versColonnes: (e) => {'id': e.id, 'nom': e.nom, 'prenom': e.prenom, 'classe_id': e.classeId},
      cle: (e) => e.id,
    );

Repository<Matiere> _repoMatiere(MySQLConnection cnx) => Repository<Matiere>(
      cnx,
      table: 'matieres',
      colonneCle: 'id',
      depuisLigne: (l) => Matiere(
        id: l.typedColByName<int>('id')!,
        nom: l.typedColByName<String>('nom')!,
        coefficient: _decimal(l, 'coefficient'),
      ),
      versColonnes: (m) => {'id': m.id, 'nom': m.nom, 'coefficient': m.coefficient},
      cle: (m) => m.id,
    );

Future<void> main() async {
  final connexion = await MySQLConnection.createConnection(
    host: 'localhost',
    port: 3306,
    userName: 'admecole',
    password: 'mdpecole',
    databaseName: 'dbecole',
  );
  await connexion.connect();
  print('Connexion à [dbecole] établie.');

  try {
    final classeRepo = _repoClasse(connexion);
    final eleveRepo = _repoEleve(connexion);
    final matiereRepo = _repoMatiere(connexion);

    // all classes
    print('Classes :');
    for (final c in await classeRepo.findAll(orderBy: 'nom asc')) {
      print('  ${c.id} ${c.nom}');
    }

    // all subjects, with their weighting factors
    print('Matières :');
    for (final m in await matiereRepo.findAll(orderBy: 'nom asc')) {
      print('  ${m.id} ${m.nom} (coefficient ${m.coefficient})');
    }

    // adding a new student to [classe1]
    final classe1 = await classeRepo.findOneByOrFail({'nom': 'classe1'});
    final nouvel = Eleve(id: 999, nom: 'Curie', prenom: 'Marie', classeId: classe1.id);
    await eleveRepo.save(nouvel);
    print('Élève ${nouvel.prenom} ${nouvel.nom} ajouté dans ${classe1.nom}.');

    // proofreading - [différence avec TypeScript] typeorm-02.ts specifies
    // `relations: { class: true }` to load the associated class at
    // at the same time as the student. [Repository.findOneBy] cannot load QUE
    // the table [eleves] (no automatic join): so we’ll
    // search for the class ourselves, using a second explicit query—
    // exactly the additional query that TypeORM triggers for
    // us behind `relations: { class: true }`, but VISIBLE here.
    final relu = await eleveRepo.findOneByOrFail({'id': 999});
    relu.classe = await classeRepo.findOneByOrFail({'id': relu.classeId});
    print('Relecture : ${relu.prenom} ${relu.nom}, classe=${relu.classe!.nom}');

    // deletion—we restore the database to the state in which we found it
    await eleveRepo.delete({'id': 999});
    print('Élève 999 supprimé.');
  } finally {
    await connexion.close();
  }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • Lines 10–17: [num _decimal(ResultSetRow ligne, String colonne) => num.parse(ligne.typedColByName<String>(colonne)!);]: [mysql_client_plus] can convert a column SQL DECIMAL (here [matieres.coefficient]) to [String] (any type, such as SQL, can be read as [String]), but it cannot convert PAS directly to [num] or [double] - [typedColByName<num>(...)] then yields [MySQLProtocolException: Cannot convert MySQL type 246 to requested type num] (246 = NEWDECIMAL, the internal type MySQL of the columns DECIMAL). The column is therefore read as [String], and then converted manually.
  • Three private functions—[_repoClasse], [_repoEleve], and [_repoMatiere]—each construct a [Repository] for one of the three entities in [dbecole]; only [_repoMatiere] uses [_decimal] for the [coefficient] column.
  • Lines 99–100: [final relu = await eleveRepo.findOneByOrFail({'id': 999}); relu.classe = await classeRepo.findOneByOrFail({'id': relu.classeId});]: whereas [typeorm-02.ts] specifies [relations: { classe: true }] to load the associated class along with the student, [Repository.findOneBy] cannot load QUE from the table [eleves] (no automatic join)—so we retrieve the class ourselves, using a second explicit query: exactly the additional query that TypeORM triggers behind the scenes, but rendered as VISIBLE here.

The result of the execution is as follows:

Connexion à [dbecole] établie.
Classes :
1 classe1
2 classe2
Matières :
1 matiere1 (coefficient 1.0)
2 matiere2 (coefficient 2.0)
Élève Marie Curie ajouté dans classe1.
Relecture : Marie Curie, classe=classe1
Élève 999 supprimé.

docs.text:
// orm_03_joined_queries.dart
// Contains databases/typeorm/typeorm-03-joined-queries.ts.
//
// Highlights the queries SQL that need to be written to retrieve
// information spread across multiple tables—which TypeORM
// does for you behind the `relations` option, via a JOINTURE SQL
// (`JOIN`). Unlike orm_02_ecole.dart (which simulated a load
// of a relationship with DEUX separate requests, to keep things simple), this file
// writes the VRAIES joins SQL—exactly what TypeORM does
// behind the scenes, but made fully visible.
//
// [différence de fond avec TypeScript] TypeORM (such as SQLAlchemy, used
// by the original Python course) does not perform lazy loading by default
// for “standard” entities: you must explicitly request the
// relations to load, using the `relations` option. Our “lightweight” ORM
// takes this principle even further, since there is no NI lazy
// "magic" relation loading: each join is
// SQL handwritten, line by line—the price to pay for not depending
// on any object-relational mapping library.
//
// [migration mysql_client_plus] as in repository.dart, the
// positional placeholders ("?") from MySQL 1 become placeholders
// NOMMÉS (":id", ":name"...), and access to the columns of a row in
// result set ([ligne.fields['x']] with mysql1) becomes a typed call
// ([ligne.typedColByName<T>('x')]).
import 'package:mysql_client_plus/mysql_client_plus.dart';
import 'entities.dart';

// reads a column SQL DECIMAL/NUMERIC (here [notes.valeur] and
// [matieres.coefficient]) as a [num]. [package:mysql_client_plus] knows
// convert a DECIMAL to [String] (any SQL file can be read
// as [String]), but not directly from PAS to [num] or [double] -
// `typedColByName<num>(...)` then raises "Cannot convert MySQL type 246 to
// requested type num" (246 = NEWDECIMAL, the internal type MySQL of the
// DECIMAL columns). We therefore read the column as [String], then
// convert it ourselves.
num _decimal(ResultSetRow ligne, String colonne) => num.parse(ligne.typedColByName<String>(colonne)!);

// students by ID, with their class (JOIN students/classes)
Future<Eleve> _eleveAvecClasse(MySQLConnection cnx, int id) async {
  final resultats = await cnx.execute(
    'select e.id as e_id, e.nom as e_nom, e.prenom as e_prenom, e.classe_id as e_classe_id, '
    'c.id as c_id, c.nom as c_nom '
    'from eleves e join classes c on e.classe_id = c.id where e.id = :id',
    {'id': id},
  );
  final ligne = resultats.rows.first;
  return Eleve(
    id: ligne.typedColByName<int>('e_id')!,
    nom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('e_nom')!,
    prenom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('e_prenom')!,
    classeId: ligne.typedColByName<int>('e_classe_id')!,
    classe: Classe(id: ligne.typedColByName<int>('c_id')!, nom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('c_nom')!),
  );
}

// class by ID, with the list of its students (JOIN classes/students)
Future<Classe> _classeAvecEleves(MySQLConnection cnx, int id) async {
  final resultats = await cnx.execute(
    'select c.id as c_id, c.nom as c_nom, e.id as e_id, e.nom as e_nom, e.prenom as e_prenom '
    'from classes c left join eleves e on e.classe_id = c.id where c.id = :id',
    {'id': id},
  );
  final premiereLigne = resultats.rows.first;
  final classe = Classe(id: premiereLigne.typedColByName<int>('c_id')!, nom: premiereLigne.typedColByName<String>('c_nom')!);
  classe.eleves = [
    for (final ligne in resultats.rows)
      Eleve(
        id: ligne.typedColByName<int>('e_id')!,
        nom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('e_nom')!,
        prenom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('e_prenom')!,
        classeId: classe.id,
      ),
  ];
  return classe;
}

// classified by NOM, with the list of its students
Future<Classe> _classeAvecElevesParNom(MySQLConnection cnx, String nom) async {
  final resultats = await cnx.execute(
    'selects c.id as c_id, c.nom as c_nom, e.id as e_id, e.nom as e_nom, e.prenom as e_prenom '
    'from classes c left join eleves e on e.classe_id = c.id where c.nom = :nom',
    {'nom': nom},
  );
  final premiereLigne = resultats.rows.first;
  final classe = Classe(id: premiereLigne.typedColByName<int>('c_id')!, nom: premiereLigne.typedColByName<String>('c_nom')!);
  classe.eleves = [
    for (final ligne in resultats.rows)
      Eleve(
        id: ligne.typedColByName<int>('e_id')!,
        nom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('e_nom')!,
        prenom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('e_prenom')!,
        classeId: classe.id,
      ),
  ];
  return classe;
}

// is a student of NOM, along with his class
Future<Eleve> _eleveParNomAvecClasse(MySQLConnection cnx, String nom) async {
  final resultats = await cnx.execute(
    'selects e.id as e_id, e.nom as e_nom, e.prenom as e_prenom, e.classe_id as e_classe_id, '
    'c.id as c_id, c.nom as c_nom '
    'from eleves e join classes c on e.classe_id = c.id where e.nom = :nom',
    {'nom': nom},
  );
  final ligne = resultats.rows.first;
  return Eleve(
    id: ligne.typedColByName<int>('e_id')!,
    nom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('e_nom')!,
    prenom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('e_prenom')!,
    classeId: ligne.typedColByName<int>('e_classe_id')!,
    classe: Classe(id: ligne.typedColByName<int>('c_id')!, nom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('c_nom')!),
  );
}

// a student's grades, with the subject for each grade (duplicate of JOIN)
Future<Eleve> _eleveAvecNotesEtMatiere(MySQLConnection cnx, int id) async {
  final ligneEleve = (await cnx.execute('select id, nom, prenom, classe_id from eleves where id = :id', {'id': id})).rows.first;
  final eleve = Eleve(
    id: ligneEleve.typedColByName<int>('id')!,
    nom: ligneEleve.typedColByName<String>('nom')!,
    prenom: ligneEleve.typedColByName<String>('prenom')!,
    classeId: ligneEleve.typedColByName<int>('classe_id')!,
  );
  final resultats = await cnx.execute(
    'select n.id as n_id, n.valeur as n_valeur, m.id as m_id, m.nom as m_nom, m.coefficient as m_coefficient '
    'from notes n join matieres m on n.matiere_id = m.id where n.eleve_id = :id',
    {'id': id},
  );
  eleve.notes = [
    for (final ligne in resultats.rows)
      Note(
        id: ligne.typedColByName<int>('n_id')!,
        valeur: _decimal(ligne, 'n_valeur'),
        eleveId: eleve.id,
        matiereId: ligne.typedColByName<int>('m_id')!,
        matiere: Matiere(
          id: ligne.typedColByName<int>('m_id')!,
          nom: ligne.typedColByName<String>('m_nom')!,
          coefficient: _decimal(ligne, 'm_coefficient'),
        ),
      ),
  ];
  return eleve;
}

// subject by NOM, with the list of its grades
Future<Matiere> _matiereAvecNotesParNom(MySQLConnection cnx, String nom) async {
  final resultats = await cnx.execute(
    'selects m.id as m_id, m.nom as m_nom, m.coefficient as m_coefficient, n.id as n_id, n.valeur as n_valeur '
    'from matieres m left join notes n on n.matiere_id = m.id where m.nom = :nom',
    {'nom': nom},
  );
  final premiereLigne = resultats.rows.first;
  final matiere = Matiere(
    id: premiereLigne.typedColByName<int>('m_id')!,
    nom: premiereLigne.typedColByName<String>('m_nom')!,
    coefficient: _decimal(premiereLigne, 'm_coefficient'),
  );
  matiere.notes = [
    for (final ligne in resultats.rows)
      Note(
        id: ligne.typedColByName<int>('n_id')!,
        valeur: _decimal(ligne, 'n_valeur'),
        eleveId: 0,
        matiereId: matiere.id,
      ),
  ];
  return matiere;
}

Future<void> main() async {
  final connexion = await MySQLConnection.createConnection(
    host: 'localhost',
    port: 3306,
    userName: 'admecole',
    password: 'mdpecole',
    databaseName: 'dbecole',
  );
  await connexion.connect();

  try {
    // student by ID, with their class (explicit join)
    print('élève id=11 -----------');
    final eleve11 = await _eleveAvecClasse(connexion, 11);
    print('élève={"id":${eleve11.id},"nom":"${eleve11.nom}","prénom":"${eleve11.prenom}"}');
    print('classe de l\'élève : {"id":${eleve11.classe!.id},"nom":"${eleve11.classe!.nom}"}');

    // students in the same class (new query, with its own
    // join)
    print('élèves dans la même classe :');
    final classeDeLeleve = await _classeAvecEleves(connexion, eleve11.classe!.id);
    for (final e in classeDeLeleve.eleves) {
      print('élève={"id":${e.id},"nom":"${e.nom}","prénom":"${e.prenom}"}');
    }

    // a student by name
    print("élève nom='nom2' -----------");
    final parNom = await _eleveParNomAvecClasse(connexion, 'nom2');
    print('élève={"id":${parNom.id},"nom":"${parNom.nom}","prénom":"${parNom.prenom}"}');
    print('classe de l\'élève : {"id":${parNom.classe!.id},"nom":"${parNom.classe!.nom}"}');

    // a student's grades, with the subject for each grade
    print("notes de l'élève id=11 -----------");
    final eleveAvecNotes = await _eleveAvecNotesEtMatiere(connexion, 11);
    for (final note in eleveAvecNotes.notes) {
      print('note={"id":${note.id},"valeur":${note.valeur}}, matière={"nom":"${note.matiere!.nom}"}');
    }

    // students in a class, by class name
    for (final nomClasse in ['classe1', 'classe2']) {
      print("élèves de la classe nom='$nomClasse' -----------");
      final classe = await _classeAvecElevesParNom(connexion, nomClasse);
      for (final e in classe.eleves) {
        print('{"id":${e.id},"nom":"${e.nom}","prénom":"${e.prenom}"}');
      }
    }

    // Grades in a subject, by subject name
    for (final nomMatiere in ['matiere1', 'matiere2']) {
      print("matière de nom='$nomMatiere' -----------");
      final matiere = await _matiereAvecNotesParNom(connexion, nomMatiere);
      print('matière={"nom":"${matiere.nom}","coefficient":${matiere.coefficient}}');
      print('Notes dans la matière : ');
      for (final note in matiere.notes) {
        print('{"id":${note.id},"valeur":${note.valeur}}');
      }
    }
  } finally {
    await connexion.close();
  }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • Unlike [orm_02_ecole.dart] (two separate requests), this file writes the VRAIES joins for SQL—exactly what TypeORM does behind the scenes via the [relations] option, but made fully visible.
  • Lines 44–61: [from eleves e join classes c on e.classe_id = c.id where e.id = :id], [from classes c left join eleves e on e.classe_id = c.id where c.id = :id]: JOIN (required relationship) and LEFT JOIN (optional relationship; a class may have no students) - the distinction that TypeORM selects for you based on the declared optionality of the relationship. The positional placeholders ([?]) from [mysql1] become NOMMÉS ([:id]) placeholders, and access to the columns of a row ([ligne['x']] or [ligne.fields['x']] with [mysql1]) becomes a typed call ([ligne.typedColByName<T>('x')]).
  • Line 135: [valeur: _decimal(ligne, 'n_valeur')], [coefficient: _decimal(ligne, 'm_coefficient')]: same helper [_decimal] as in [orm_02_ecole.dart], required here for the two columns DECIMAL, [notes.valeur], and [matieres.coefficient].
  • TypeORM (like SQLAlchemy) does not perform lazy loading by default on “standard” entities: you must explicitly request the relationships using the [relations] option. The lightweight ORM takes this principle even further, since there is no lazy loading here—no “magical” relation loading: each join is hand-written—the price to pay for not depending on any object-relational mapping library.

docs.text:
// orm_04_stats.dart
// Database: databases/typeorm/typeorm-04-stats.ts.
//
// Calculates, for a given student, their grade point average weighted by the coefficients
// subjects, as well as the minimum and maximum grades.
//
// [différence avec TypeScript] typeorm-04-stats.ts warned that the
// `decimal` columns in MySQL (here, note.valeur and matiere.coefficient)
// are returned by the mysql2 driver as CHAÎNES DE
// CARACTÈRES at runtime (to avoid losing precision), despite their
// declared type `number`—a classic pitfall of TypeScript, where the
// static type may not reflect the actual value at runtime. On the Dart side,
// [package:mysql_client_plus] has a similar pitfall, but it is handled by the
// compiler rather than hidden at runtime: the typed access
// (`typedColByName<T>(...)`) cannot convert a column DECIMAL
// (internal type SQL 246, "NEWDECIMAL")—neither to [num] nor to [double]—it
// raises `MySQLProtocolException: Cannot convert MySQL type 246 to requested
// type num`. The only guaranteed conversion for N'IMPORTE QUEL type SQL is
// [String]; therefore, the columns DECIMAL are read as [String] with
// `typedColByName<String>(...)`, and then we convert them ourselves using
// [num.parse]—see [_decimal] below.
import 'package:mysql_client_plus/mysql_client_plus.dart';

// reads a column SQL DECIMAL/NUMERIC as a [num] (see comment on
// file header)
num _decimal(ResultSetRow ligne, String colonne) => num.parse(ligne.typedColByName<String>(colonne)!);

// calculates the statistics (weighted average, minimum, maximum) for a student
Future<void> _statsEleve(MySQLConnection cnx, int idEleve) async {
  final eleveLigne = (await cnx.execute('select id, nom, prenom from eleves where id = :id', {'id': idEleve})).rows.first;
  print(
    'Student statistics {"id":${eleveLigne.typedColByName<int>('id')},"last_name":"${eleveLigne.typedColByName<String>('last_name')}",""first_name":"${eleveLigne.typedColByName<String>('first_name')}"}',
  );

  final notes = await cnx.execute(
    'select n.valeur as value, m.nom as matiere_nom, m.coefficient as coefficient '
    'from notes n join matieres m on n.matiere_id = m.id where n.eleve_id = :id',
    {'id': idEleve},
  );

  if (notes.rows.isEmpty) {
    print('  aucune note.');
    return;
  }

  num sommePonderee = 0;
  num sommeCoefficients = 0;
  num mini = double.infinity;
  num maxi = double.negativeInfinity;

  for (final ligne in notes.rows) {
    // explicit conversion via [_decimal] (see note at the top of the file):
    // [valeur] and [coefficient] are therefore valid [num] values, not strings
    final valeur = _decimal(ligne, 'valeur');
    final coefficient = _decimal(ligne, 'coefficient');
    sommePonderee += valeur * coefficient;
    sommeCoefficients += coefficient;
    if (valeur < mini) mini = valeur;
    if (valeur > maxi) maxi = valeur;
    print(
      ' note=${valeur.toStringAsFixed(2)} subject="${ligne.typedColByName<String>('matiere_nom')}" '
      '(weighting factor ${coefficient.toStringAsFixed(2)})',
    );
  }

  final moyenne = sommePonderee / sommeCoefficients;
  print('  moyenne pondérée=${moyenne.toStringAsFixed(2)}, mini=${mini.toStringAsFixed(2)}, maxi=${maxi.toStringAsFixed(2)}');
}

Future<void> main() async {
  final connexion = await MySQLConnection.createConnection(
    host: 'localhost',
    port: 3306,
    userName: 'admecole',
    password: 'mdpecole',
    databaseName: 'dbecole',
  );
  await connexion.connect();

  try {
    // student id=11: grades for subject1=10 (weight 1.0), subject2=6 (weight 2.0)
    // weighted average = (10*1.0 + 6*2.0) / (1.0+2.0) = 22/3 = 7.33
    await _statsEleve(connexion, 11);
    print('');
    // student ID=21: grades for subject1=12 (weight 1.0), subject2=8 (weight 2.0)
    await _statsEleve(connexion, 21);
    print('');
    // student ID=32: grades for subject1=14 (weight 1.0), subject2=10 (weight 2.0)
    await _statsEleve(connexion, 32);
    print('');
    // student ID=42: grades for subject1=16 (weight 1.0), subject2=12 (weight 2.0)
    await _statsEleve(connexion, 42);
  } finally {
    await connexion.close();
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • [typeorm-04-stats.ts] indicated that the columns [decimal] from MySQL (in this case, [note.valeur] and [matiere.coefficient]) are returned by [mysql2] as CHAÎNES, DE, and CARACTÈRES at runtime (to avoid losing precision), despite their declared type being [number]—a classic pitfall of TypeScript, where the static type may not reflect the actual value at runtime.
  • Line 26: [num _decimal(ResultSetRow ligne, String colonne) => num.parse(ligne.typedColByName<String>(colonne)!);]: on the Dart side, [package:mysql_client_plus] has a pitfall similar to that of TypeScript, but is rendered as VISIBLE by the compiler rather than hidden at runtime: the typed access ([typedColByName<T>(...)]) cannot convert a column DECIMAL to either [num] or [double] - it raises [MySQLProtocolException: Cannot convert MySQL type 246 to requested type num]. The only guaranteed conversion for any SQL type is to [String]; so the columns labeled DECIMAL are read as [String], and then converted manually to [num.parse].
  • Line 67: [final moyenne = sommePonderee / sommeCoefficients;]: The weighted average calculation itself is identical to the TypeScript version and the [mysql1] version—only the LECTURE value in the DECIMAL columns has changed.
