docs.title: 7.2.7. What the lightweight ORM does not do
docs.text: Unlike TypeORM/Prisma: no schema generation ([synchronize]/migrations), no decorators, no lazy loading or identity cache, no query builder ([QueryBuilder]), and loading a relationship is TOUJOURS a second query or a hand-written join—never automatic. This is a deliberate compromise: enough to illustrate the repository pattern using the example from the course, without claiming to replace a real repository in production.

docs.title: 6. HTTP clients for the tax calculation service
6.1. Introduction
docs.text: This chapter reproduces, without any structural changes, the three successive layers of clients built in the TypeScript course, each refining the previous one: a first client, CLI, where all calculations remain on the server side; a second client, CLI, where the calculation moves to the client side ([métier] layer); a third client, compiled for NAVIGATEUR; and finally, a complete client, HTML, with its own views. All four rely on the same NestJS server, which was installed in the previous chapter.

docs.title: 6.2.2. [dao1] script
docs.text:
// dao1.dart
// Port Dao1.ts: The [dao] layer (Data Access Object) encapsulates all
// communication details (HTTP) with the tax calculation server (URL,
// method, session cookie) behind simple business methods
// (initSession, authentifierUtilisateur, calculerImpot...).
import 'package:dio/dio.dart';

class Dao1 {
  final Dio _dio;
  final String _sessionCookieName;
  String _sessionCookie = '';

  // constructor—receives the Dio instance to be used, just like the script
  // TypeScript received the axios instance as a parameter
  Dao1(this._dio) : _sessionCookieName = "connect.sid";

  // init session
  Future<dynamic> initSession() {
    return _getRemoteData(
      'main.php',
      method: 'GET',
      queryParameters: {'action': 'init-session', 'type': 'json'},
    );
  }

  Future<dynamic> authentifierUtilisateur(String user, String password) {
    return _getRemoteData(
      'main.php',
      method: 'POST',
      queryParameters: {'action': 'authentifier-utilisateur'},
      data: {'user': user, 'password': password},
      contentType: Headers.formUrlEncodedContentType,
    );
  }

  // tax calculation
  Future<dynamic> calculerImpot(String marie, int enfants, int salaire) {
    return _getRemoteData(
      'main.php',
      method: 'POST',
      queryParameters: {'action': 'calculer-impot'},
      data: {'marié': marie, 'enfants': enfants, 'salaire': salaire},
      contentType: Headers.formUrlEncodedContentType,
    );
  }

  // list of simulations
  Future<dynamic> listeSimulations() {
    return _getRemoteData(
      'main.php',
      method: 'GET',
      queryParameters: {'action': 'lister-simulations'},
    );
  }

  // delete a simulation
  Future<dynamic> supprimerSimulation(int index) {
    return _getRemoteData(
      'main.php',
      method: 'GET',
      queryParameters: {'action': 'supprimer-simulation', 'numéro': index},
    );
  }

  Future<dynamic> _getRemoteData(
    String path, {
    required String method,
    Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,
    Object? data,
    String? contentType,
  }) async {
    // for the session cookie
    final options = Options(
      method: method,
      contentType: contentType,
      headers: {'Cookie': _sessionCookie},
      validateStatus: (_) => true,
    );
    // execute the HTTP request
    final response = await _dio.request(
      path,
      queryParameters: queryParameters,
      data: data,
      options: options,
    );
    // retrieve the session cookie if it exists
    final setCookie = response.headers['set-cookie'];
    if (setCookie != null) {
      for (final entete in setCookie) {
        final resultat = RegExp('^($_sessionCookieName.+?);').firstMatch(entete);
        if (resultat != null) {
          _sessionCookie = resultat.group(1)!;
          break;
        }
      }
    }
    // the server's response is in [response.data]
    return response.data;
  }
}

Let's comment on this code:

  • Line 48: The [dao] layer (Data Access Object) encapsulates all HTTP communication details (URL, method, session cookie) behind simple business methods - [initSession], [authentifierUtilisateur], [calculerImpot], [listeSimulations], [supprimerSimulation] (line 57).
  • Line 15: [Dao1(this._dio)] receives the [Dio] instance to be used as a constructor parameter, exactly as the TypeScript script received the [axios] instance.
  • Line 87: [_getRemoteData] (private, prefix [_]) centralizes manual tracking of the session cookie ([response.headers['set-cookie']], [RegExp] (line 90)) already encountered in dart_dio_03.dart: each public method of DAO relies on this same private method.

// main1.dart
// Port main1.ts.
import 'dart:convert';
import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
import 'dao1.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  // Dio configuration - baseUrl/global timeouts, such as axios.defaults in
  // TypeScript
  final dio = Dio(BaseOptions(
    baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3000/',
    connectTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 2),
    receiveTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 2),
  ));
  // instantiation of the [dao] layer
  final dao = Dao1(dio);
  // using the [dao] layer
  try {
    // session initialization
    log("-----------init-session");
    dynamic response = await dao.initSession();
    log(response);
    // authentication
    log("-----------authentifier-utilisateur");
    response = await dao.authentifierUtilisateur("admin", "admin");
    log(response);
    // tax calculations - Future.wait is the Dart equivalent of Promise.all
    // (already seen in async_05.dart)
    log("-----------calculer-impot x 3");
    response = await Future.wait([
      dao.calculerImpot("oui", 2, 45000),
      dao.calculerImpot("non", 2, 45000),
      dao.calculerImpot("non", 1, 30000),
    ]);
    log(response);
    // list of simulations
    log("-----------liste-des-simulations");
    response = await dao.listeSimulations();
    log(response);
    // deleting a simulation
    log("-----------suppression simulation n° 1");
    response = await dao.supprimerSimulation(1);
    log(response);
  } catch (erreur) {
    // logs the error
    print("erreur=$erreur");
  }
}

// log jSON
void log(Object? object) {
  const JsonEncoder encoder = JsonEncoder.withIndent('  ');
  print(encoder.convert(object));
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 16: [final dao = Dao1(dio);]: the [dao] layer is instantiated only once, then reused for the entire sequence of calls (init-session, authentication, calculations, list, deletion).
  • Lines 30–31: [Future.wait([dao.calculerImpot(...), ...])]: the three tax calculations are launched: EN and PARALLÈLE, the Dart equivalent of [Promise.all], which was already encountered in async_05.dart.
  • Lines 52–53: [JsonEncoder.withIndent(' ').convert(object)]: The utility function [log] replicates the indexed display of [JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)].

docs.title: 6.3. Client HTTP 2
docs.text: This second client moves the CALCUL tax data from the server to the client: the server now provides the raw tax data (rates, thresholds, etc.) only once via [get-admindata], and the [métier] layer now performs the calculations.

docs.title: 6.3.2. script [metier]
docs.text:
// metier.dart
// Port Metier.ts: tax calculation, performed entirely on the client side
// (in the browser as TypeScript, here in the Dart program), based on
// the raw tax data retrieved once from the server via
// [Dao2.getAdminData] (see dao2.dart).
class Metier {
  // [dynamic]: The exact structure of the tax data sent by the server
  // tax-related data (rates, thresholds, etc.) is not documented here; as in
  // TypeScript, we are deliberately keeping things flexible regarding this type
  final Map<String, dynamic> taxAdminData;

  Metier(this.taxAdminData);

  // tax calculation
  // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // married: yes, no
  // children: number of children
  // salary: annual salary
  Map<String, dynamic> calculerImpot(String marie, int enfants, num salaire) {
    // tax calculation with children
    final result1 = _calculerImpot2(marie, enfants, salaire);
    final impot1 = result1['impôt'] as num;
    // Tax calculation without children
    Map<String, dynamic> result2;
    num impot2;
    num plafondDemiPart;
    if (enfants != 0) {
      result2 = _calculerImpot2(marie, 0, salaire);
      impot2 = result2['impôt'] as num;
      // Application of the family quotient cap
      plafondDemiPart = taxAdminData['plafondQfDemiPart'] as num;
      if (enfants < 3) {
        // plafondDemiPart for the first 2 children
        impot2 = impot2 - enfants * plafondDemiPart;
      } else {
        // plafondDemiPart for the first 2 children, double that amount for subsequent children
        impot2 = impot2 - 2 * plafondDemiPart - (enfants - 2) * 2 * plafondDemiPart;
      }
    } else {
      // no tax recalculation
      impot2 = impot1;
      result2 = result1;
    }
    // the highest tax amount is used from [impot1, impot2]
    num impot;
    num taux;
    num surcote;
    if (impot1 > impot2) {
      impot = impot1;
      taux = result1['taux'] as num;
      surcote = result1['surcôte'] as num;
    } else {
      surcote = impot2 - impot1 + (result2['surcôte'] as num);
      impot = impot2;
      taux = result2['taux'] as num;
    }
    // calculation of a possible tax deduction
    final decote = _getDecote(marie, impot);
    impot -= decote;
    // Calculation of a potential tax reduction
    final reduction = _getReduction(marie, salaire, enfants, impot);
    impot -= reduction;
    // Result
    return {
      'impôt': impot.floor(),
      'surcôte': surcote,
      'décôte': decote,
      'réduction': reduction,
      'taux': taux,
    };
  }

  // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Map<String, dynamic> _calculerImpot2(String marie, int enfants, num salaire) {
    // number of shares
    marie = marie.toLowerCase();
    num nbParts;
    if (marie == "oui") {
      nbParts = enfants / 2 + 2;
    } else {
      nbParts = enfants / 2 + 1;
    }
    // 1 share per child starting with the third
    if (enfants >= 3) {
      // half an additional share for each child starting with the third
      nbParts += 0.5 * (enfants - 2);
    }
    // taxable income
    final revenuImposable = _getRevenuImposable(salaire);
    // surcharge
    num surcote = (revenuImposable - 0.9 * salaire).floor();
    // for rounding issues
    if (surcote < 0) {
      surcote = 0;
    }
    // family quotient
    final quotient = revenuImposable / nbParts;
    // tax calculation
    final List<num> limites = List<num>.from(taxAdminData['limites'] as List);
    final List<num> coeffR = List<num>.from(taxAdminData['coeffR'] as List);
    final List<num> coeffN = List<num>.from(taxAdminData['coeffN'] as List);
    //is placed at the end of the list [limites] to stop the following loop
    limites[limites.length - 1] = quotient;
    // lookup of tax rate
    var i = 0;
    while (quotient > limites[i]) {
      i++;
    }
    // Since the quotient was placed at the end of the limits, the loop
    // cannot overflow the limits list
    // Now we can calculate the tax
    final impot = (revenuImposable * coeffR[i] - nbParts * coeffN[i]).floor();
    // Result
    return {'impôt': impot, 'surcôte': surcote, 'taux': coeffR[i]};
  }

  // revenuImposable = salaireAnnuel - tax deduction (the tax deduction has a minimum and a maximum)
  num _getRevenuImposable(num salaire) {
    // 10% pay cut
    num abattement = 0.1 * salaire;
    // this deduction cannot exceed abattementDixPourCentMax
    final abattementMax = taxAdminData['abattementDixPourCentMax'] as num;
    if (abattement > abattementMax) {
      abattement = abattementMax;
    }
    // The deduction cannot be less than abattementDixPourcentMin
    final abattementMin = taxAdminData['abattementDixPourcentMin'] as num;
    if (abattement < abattementMin) {
      abattement = abattementMin;
    }
    // taxable income
    final revenuImposable = salaire - abattement;
    return revenuImposable.floor();
  }

  // calculates any discount
  num _getDecote(String marie, num impots) {
    // Initially, a zero discount
    num decote = 0;
    // maximum tax amount to qualify for the discount
    final plafondImpotPourDecote = marie == "oui"
        ? taxAdminData['plafondImpotCouplePourDecote'] as num
        : taxAdminData['plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote'] as num;
    if (impots < plafondImpotPourDecote) {
      // maximum discount amount
      final plafondDecote = marie == "oui"
          ? taxAdminData['plafondDecoteCouple'] as num
          : taxAdminData['plafondDecoteCelibataire'] as num;
      // theoretical discount
      decote = plafondDecote - 0.75 * impots;
      // The discount cannot exceed the tax amount
      if (decote > impots) {
        decote = impots;
      }
      // no discount < 0
      if (decote < 0) {
        decote = 0;
      }
    }
    // Result: `ceil()` is the Dart equivalent of `Math.ceil()`
    return decote.ceil();
  }

  // Calculates a potential reduction
  num _getReduction(String marie, num salaire, int enfants, num impots) {
    // the income threshold for eligibility for the 20% reduction
    num plafondRevenuPourReduction = marie == "oui"
        ? taxAdminData['plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction'] as num
        : taxAdminData['plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction'] as num;
    final valeurReducDemiPart = taxAdminData['valeurReducDemiPart'] as num;
    plafondRevenuPourReduction += enfants * valeurReducDemiPart;
    if (enfants > 2) {
      plafondRevenuPourReduction += (enfants - 2) * valeurReducDemiPart;
    }
    // taxable income
    final revenuImposable = _getRevenuImposable(salaire);
    // reduction
    num reduction = 0;
    if (revenuImposable < plafondRevenuPourReduction) {
      // 20% reduction
      reduction = 0.2 * impots;
    }
    return reduction.ceil();
  }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 12: [Metier(this.taxAdminData)]: the constructor receives the raw tax data retrieved by DAO only once—no further network calls are required afterward to calculate a tax.
  • line 19: [Map<String, dynamic> calculerImpot(String marie, int enfants, num salaire)]: a faithful, line-by-line port of the TypeScript algorithm—same steps ([_calculerImpot2], [_getRevenuImposable], [_getDecote], [_getReduction]), same logic for capping the family quotient.
  • [.floor()]/[.ceil()] (methods of [num]) replace [Math.floor(...)]/[Math.ceil(...)]: In Dart, these are instance methods on the number itself, not static methods of a utility class.
  • The CLÉS instances of the rendered [Map] ([impot], [surcote]...) remain accented ([impôt], [surcôte], [décôte], [réduction]): only the IDENTIFIANTS Dart (variable and parameter names) are unaccented—a string can still contain accents in Dart (see simulation.dart, later in this chapter).

docs.text:
// dao2.dart
// Key Dao2.ts: identical to dao1.dart for initSession and
// authentifierUtilisateur, but displays [getAdminData] instead of
// [calculerImpot]/[listeSimulations]/[supprimerSimulation]—the calculation and
// the list of simulations are now managed on the CLIENT side by the layer
// [métier] layer (see metier.dart); the server is now used solely to provide the
// raw tax data (rates, thresholds, etc.).
import 'package:dio/dio.dart';

class Dao2 {
  final Dio _dio;
  final String _sessionCookieName;
  String _sessionCookie = '';

  Dao2(this._dio) : _sessionCookieName = "connect.sid";

  Future<dynamic> initSession() {
    return _getRemoteData(
      'main.php',
      method: 'GET',
      queryParameters: {'action': 'init-session', 'type': 'json'},
    );
  }

  Future<dynamic> authentifierUtilisateur(String user, String password) {
    return _getRemoteData(
      'main.php',
      method: 'POST',
      queryParameters: {'action': 'authentifier-utilisateur'},
      data: {'user': user, 'password': password},
      contentType: Headers.formUrlEncodedContentType,
    );
  }

  Future<dynamic> getAdminData() {
    return _getRemoteData(
      'main.php',
      method: 'GET',
      queryParameters: {'action': 'get-admindata'},
    );
  }

  Future<dynamic> _getRemoteData(
    String path, {
    required String method,
    Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,
    Object? data,
    String? contentType,
  }) async {
    final options = Options(
      method: method,
      contentType: contentType,
      headers: {'Cookie': _sessionCookie},
      validateStatus: (_) => true,
    );
    final response = await _dio.request(
      path,
      queryParameters: queryParameters,
      data: data,
      options: options,
    );
    final setCookie = response.headers['set-cookie'];
    if (setCookie != null) {
      for (final entete in setCookie) {
        final resultat = RegExp('^($_sessionCookieName.+?);').firstMatch(entete);
        if (resultat != null) {
          _sessionCookie = resultat.group(1)!;
          break;
        }
      }
    }
    return response.data;
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 4: Identical to [Dao1] for [initSession] and [authentifierUtilisateur], but exposes [getAdminData] instead of [calculerImpot]/[listeSimulations] (line 4)/[supprimerSimulation] (line 4): These three operations are now handled on the CLIENT side by the [métier] layer that was just introduced.

docs.title: 6.4.1. Evolution of the toolkit since 2019
docs.text: This third client uses the same [dao]/[métier] pair as client HTTP 2, but uses COMPILÉ, POUR, LE, and NAVIGATEUR instead of being run from the command line. As for TypeScript, this build requires webpack and babel, as well as polyfills ([core-js/stable], [regenerator-runtime/runtime]) so that modern code works in older browsers. On the Dart side, SDK provides its own web compiler ([dart compile js]): no polyfills are needed; [Future]/[async]/[await], records, patterns, etc., are compiled directly to the equivalent JavaScript, regardless of the target.

docs.title: 6.4.2. Compiling and Running the Project
docs.text:
From the [client http 3] folder:

The [webdev serve] development server is not provided by the SDK Dart package: the [webdev] package must first be installed once, globally, using [dart pub global activate webdev].

This command installs the [webdev] executable in the global pub cache, a folder that is not automatically created in the Windows PATH directory. To add it there once and for all (as the current user), open a PowerShell terminal and run:

[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", $env:Path + ";$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Pub\Cache\bin", "User")

You must then close and reopen the terminal (or VSCode) for the new PATH to take effect. Then, still in the [client http 3] folder:

dart pub get
webdev serve

In development, [webdev serve] launches a server that automatically recompiles with every change (hot reload): the terminal displays the URL to open in a browser (default: http://localhost:8080). For a production build, the [dart compile js index.dart -o dist/main.dart.js] command remains available: a minimal HTML page then loads [dist/main.dart.js] to test the result—the same concept as the minimal entry point [src/index.ts] in the TypeScript course.

docs.title: 6.4.4. script [main3]
docs.text:
// main3.dart
// Gate main3.ts.
//
// [ATTENTION, différence de fond avec TypeScript] main3.ts needed
// two polyfills (core-js/stable, regenerator-runtime) so that
// async/await and recent features JavaScript work on
// older browsers, once transpiled by Babel/Webpack. The
// Dart compiler for the web (`dart compile js`) does not require AUCUN
// polyfills such as Future/async/await, Records, and patterns...
// are compiled directly to JavaScript or WebAssembly
// equivalent, regardless of the target—a direct benefit of compiling
// from a unified language and toolset, rather than transpilating
// "modern" JavaScript to "legacy" JavaScript.
import 'dart:convert';
import 'package:http/browser_client.dart';
import 'dao3.dart';
import 'metier.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  // browser-specific HTTP client, with withCredentials=true -
  // the Dart equivalent of "axios.defaults.withCredentials=true"
  final client = BrowserClient()..withCredentials = true;
  final dao = Dao3(client, 'http://localhost:3000');

  Map<String, dynamic> taxAdminData;
  try {
    log("-----------init-session");
    Map<String, dynamic> response = await dao.initSession();
    log(response);
    if (response['état'] != 700) {
      throw Exception(jsonEncode(response['réponse']));
    }
    log("-----------authentifier-utilisateur");
    response = await dao.authentifierUtilisateur("admin", "admin");
    log(response);
    if (response['état'] != 200) {
      throw Exception(jsonEncode(response['réponse']));
    }
    log("-----------get-admindata");
    response = await dao.getAdminData();
    log(response);
    if (response['état'] != 1000) {
      throw Exception(jsonEncode(response['réponse']));
    }
    taxAdminData = response['réponse'] as Map<String, dynamic>;
  } catch (erreur) {
    print("erreur=$erreur");
    return;
  } finally {
    client.close();
  }

  // instantiating the [métier] layer
  final metier = Metier(taxAdminData);

  log("-----------calculer-impot x 3");
  final List<Map<String, dynamic>> simulations = [];
  simulations.add(metier.calculerImpot("oui", 2, 45000));
  simulations.add(metier.calculerImpot("non", 2, 45000));
  simulations.add(metier.calculerImpot("non", 1, 30000));
  log("-----------liste-des-simulations");
  log(simulations);
  log("-----------suppression simulation n° 1");
  simulations.removeAt(1);
  log(simulations);
}

// log jSON
void log(Object? object) {
  const JsonEncoder encoder = JsonEncoder.withIndent('  ');
  print(encoder.convert(object));
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 22: [final client = BrowserClient()..withCredentials = true;]: [BrowserClient] ([package:http/browser_client.dart]) does not exist when the code is compiled for the web; its option [withCredentials] is the Dart equivalent of [axios.defaults.withCredentials = true]—NAVIGATEUR then handles the session cookie on its own.
  • The Dart web compiler does not require the AUCUN polyfill (unlike main3.ts): [Future]/[async]/[await], and recent language features are compiled directly—a direct benefit of starting with a unified language and toolset rather than transpiling from modern JavaScript to legacy JavaScript.

docs.title: 6.4.6. [dao3] script
docs.text:
// dao3.dart
// Tax/Customer HTTP Client 3/src/Dao3.ts.
//
// Difference from dao2.dart: this file is intended to be compiled for the
// NAVIGATEUR (using `dart compile js`, see README in this folder), not
// run in CLI with `dart run`. In a browser, the COOKIE DE SESSION
// is automatically handled by the browser itself (as with any
// web page) as long as you allow them to be sent—so there is no longer
// need to manually track the cookie in MANUEL at dao1.dart/dao2.dart
// (exactly the same reasoning, already in place, that allowed Dao3.ts to
// remove all cookie management code from Dao2.ts).
//
// [correspondance avec TypeScript] "axios.defaults.withCredentials = true"
// (defined in main3.dart, not here) corresponds, on the Dart package side [http], to
// the web-specific client option [withCredentials],
// [BrowserClient] (package:http/browser_client.dart) — a class that
// does not exist (QUE) when the code is compiled for the web, unlike
// http.Client, which works everywhere.
import 'dart:convert';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

class Dao3 {
  final http.Client _client;
  final String _baseUrl;

  Dao3(this._client, this._baseUrl);

  Future<dynamic> initSession() {
    return _getRemoteData(
      'main.php',
      method: 'GET',
      queryParameters: {'action': 'init-session', 'type': 'json'},
    );
  }

  Future<dynamic> authentifierUtilisateur(String user, String password) {
    return _getRemoteData(
      'main.php',
      method: 'POST',
      queryParameters: {'action': 'authentifier-utilisateur'},
      body: {'user': user, 'password': password},
    );
  }

  Future<dynamic> getAdminData() {
    return _getRemoteData(
      'main.php',
      method: 'GET',
      queryParameters: {'action': 'get-admindata'},
    );
  }

  Future<dynamic> _getRemoteData(
    String path, {
    required String method,
    Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,
    Map<String, String>? body,
  }) async {
    final uri = Uri.parse('$_baseUrl/$path').replace(
      queryParameters: queryParameters?.map((k, v) => MapEntry(k, '$v')),
    );
    final http.Response response;
    if (method == 'POST') {
      response = await _client.post(uri, body: body);
    } else {
      response = await _client.get(uri);
    }
    // [différence avec le client CLI] no manual reading of the header
    // set-cookie here: in a browser, response.headers doesn't expose it
    // not even that (header protected by the browser, invisible to the code
    // JavaScript/Dart, precisely because it is already handled automatically)
    return jsonDecode(response.body);
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • In addition to AUCUN, manual tracking of the session cookie (unlike [Dao1]/[Dao2]): In a browser, the session cookie is managed automatically by the browser itself, provided that sending cookies is allowed ([withCredentials], set in main3.dart).
  • [response.headers] no longer even exposes the [set-cookie] header in a browser: a protected header, invisible to the client-side JavaScript/Dart code, precisely because it is already managed on its own.

docs.title: 6.5.1. Solution Architecture
docs.text: This fourth and final client adds a true HTML interface on top of client HTTP 3: the [dao] ([Dao3]) and [métier] ([Metier]) are REPRISES, SANS, and MODIFICATION, and two new layers are added—VUES (DOM build) and CONTRÔLEUR (orchestration). The project is organized into two folders, [web/] (entry point, HTML, CSS) and [lib/] (shared code), following the convention of a standard Dart web project—see README.md in this folder for details on this convention.

docs.title: 6.5.2. The HTML template: the [web/index.html] file
docs.text: Copied exactly from [src/index.html] (same classes as CSS: [bandeau], [menu], [contenu], [titre-section], [ligne-champ], [resultat], [erreur], [simulations]...), with one small difference: the script being loaded is [main.dart.js] (named FIXE by the Dart web tool), whereas [index.html] from Vues.ts loaded a Webpack bundle named HASHÉ ([main.a44f6e1c12ab338daedc.js]).

docs.title: 6.5.3. The modified [webpack.config.js] configuration
docs.text: No equivalent is needed on the Dart side: no bundler configuration file needs to be written. [web/main.dart], by virtue of its sole POSITION in the directory tree (directly under [web/]), the role that the [entry: './src/main3.ts'] line played for [webpack.config.js]—a naming and location convention replaces an entire configuration file.

docs.title: 6.5.4. The layers [dao] and [métier]: two files reused without modification
docs.text: [lib/dao3.dart] and [lib/metier.dart] are copies of EXACTES, which are copies of the files of the same name from client HTTP 3 - the same reuse, without any modifications, as that performed by Vues.ts and AppHtml.ts on [Dao3.ts] and [Metier.ts].

docs.title: 6.5.6. [simulation, vues] scripts
docs.text:
The views layer is supported by TROIS files: simulation.dart (the displayed data), vues.dart (the construction of DOM), and app_html.dart (the controller, discussed in the next section). Let’s start with simulation.dart:

// simulation.dart
// The result of a tax calculation, as returned by metier.dart, supplemented
// with the entered parameters. Uses the [Simulation] interface from Vues.ts.
//
// [NOUVEAU, Dart 3]—here we use a named RECORD (see
// dart-fundamentals/dart3/dart3_01_records.dart) rather than a class: a
//—a simple alias of type [typedef], with no constructor or separate file to
// to write, for data that is simply a “collection” of fields, with
// any associated behavior—exactly in the spirit of the
// TypeScript.
//
// [NOTE sur les noms de champs] unlike TypeScript/JavaScript, where
// an identifier can contain accented letters (“marié,” “impôt”—
// used throughout the original course), Dart reserves the
// identifiers for the letters ASCII: accents are only allowed in
// the CHAÎNES, DE, and CARACTÈRES (which is what metier.dart does; its Map keys
// "tax," "discount," etc., remain accented), never in a
// variable, field, class, or record name. That is why this course
// consistently uses names without accents (marie, impot, decote...)
// for everything related to IDENTIFIANT Dart.
typedef Simulation = ({
  String marie,
  int enfants,
  num salaire,
  num impot,
  num surcote,
  num decote,
  num reduction,
  num taux,
});

Let’s break down this code:

  • lines 21–24: [typedef Simulation = ({String marie, int enfants, num salaire, ...});]: whereas Vues.ts declared a INTERFACE [Simulation], this file uses a RECORD NOMMÉ Dart 3 (see dart3_01_records.dart)—a simple type alias, with no constructor or separate file, for purely descriptive data.
  • Field names are always DÉSACCENTUÉS ([marie], [impot], [decote]...) : Dart IDENTIFIANTS names are reserved for the letters ASCII, unlike TypeScript/JavaScript, where [marié]/[impôt] are valid field names.

[lib/vues.dart], which is composed of DOM and [package:web]:

// vues.dart
// Porte Vues.ts: building the views (DOM) of the application—authentication view
// authentication, tax calculation view, simulation list view. This
// module makes no network calls: it builds the DOM and delegates
// user actions to callback functions provided by the
// controller (see app_html.dart).
//
// [choix technique]—here we use [package:web] (pub.dev/packages/web),
// the modern replacement for the old `dart:html`: it exposes a API DOM that is very
// close to the standard DOM used by Vues.ts (document.createElement,
// .textContent, .addEventListener...). One key difference
// to note: a Dart event handler (a simple function) must
// be converted to a function JavaScript with [.toJS] (extension of
// dart:js_interop) before transitioning to [addEventListener]—the "bridge"
// between the Dart world and the JavaScript world, made explicit, whereas
// TypeScript requires no conversion (everything is already there from
// JavaScript).
import 'dart:js_interop';
import 'package:web/web.dart' as web;
import 'simulation.dart';

// a generic decoration (not the photo from the original PHP server)
const String _logoSvg = '''
<svg width="60" height="60" viewBox="0 0 60 60" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <circle cx="30" cy="30" r="29" fill="#eef1ec" stroke="#ccc" />
  <g fill="none" stroke="#8a9a7a" stroke-width="2">
    <path d="M30 46 C30 32 22 28 17 19" />
    <path d="M30 46 C30 30 39 26 44 17" />
    <path d="M30 46 C30 37 30 30 30 21" />
  </g>
  <g fill="#b9c9a6">
    <circle cx="17" cy="19" r="4.5" />
    <circle cx="44" cy="17" r="4.5" />
    <circle cx="30" cy="19" r="4.5" />
  </g>
</svg>''';

// view callbacks [authentification] - [différence avec TypeScript]
// A callback interface TypeScript naturally translates to a
// RECORD set of functions in Dart (see simulation.dart): lighter than a
// class, for a simple group of functions
typedef CallbacksAuthentification = ({void Function(String user, String password) onValider});

typedef CallbacksCalcul = ({
  void Function(String marie, int enfants, int salaire) onValider,
  void Function() onListe,
  void Function() onFinSession,
});

typedef CallbacksListe = ({
  void Function(int numero) onSupprimer,
  void Function() onCalcul,
  void Function() onFinSession,
});

class Vues {
  final web.HTMLElement racine;
  late web.HTMLDivElement _bandeau;
  late web.HTMLDivElement _menu;
  late web.HTMLDivElement _contenu;

  // builds the fixed page structure (header + menu/content area)
  // inside the [racine] element
  Vues(this.racine) {
    // [ATTENTION] unlike ordinary DOM properties (textContent,
    // value...), the setter [innerHTML] from package:web expects a [JSAny], not
    // a [String] Raw Dart—a characteristic of its generation related to
    // the WebIDL [LegacyNullToEmptyString] attribute of the DOM standard: it is necessary to
    // therefore always convert using [.toJS].
    racine.innerHTML = ''.toJS;

    _bandeau = _div()..className = 'bandeau';
    final logo = _div()..className = 'logo';
    logo.innerHTML = _logoSvg.toJS;
    final titre = web.document.createElement('h1') as web.HTMLHeadingElement;
    titre.textContent = 'Calculez votre impôt';
    _bandeau
      ..appendChild(logo)
      ..appendChild(titre);

    final corps = _div()..className = 'corps';
    _menu = _div()..className = 'menu';
    _contenu = _div()..className = 'contenu';
    corps
      ..appendChild(_menu)
      ..appendChild(_contenu);

    racine
      ..appendChild(_bandeau)
      ..appendChild(corps);
  }

  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  // DOM construction tools
  // --------------------------------------------------------------------

  web.HTMLDivElement _div() => web.document.createElement('div') as web.HTMLDivElement;

  void _viderMenu() {
    _menu.innerHTML = ''.toJS;
    _menu.style.display = 'none';
    _contenu.classList.add('pleine-largeur');
  }

  web.HTMLAnchorElement _lienMenu(String texte, void Function() onClick) {
    final a = web.document.createElement('a') as web.HTMLAnchorElement;
    a.textContent = texte;
    a.addEventListener('click', ((web.Event event) => onClick()).toJS);
    return a;
  }

  void _afficherMenu(List<web.HTMLAnchorElement> liens) {
    _menu.innerHTML = ''.toJS;
    _menu.style.display = '';
    _contenu.classList.remove('pleine-largeur');
    for (final lien in liens) {
      _menu.appendChild(lien);
    }
  }

  web.HTMLElement? _banniereErreur(String? message) {
    if (message == null) return null;
    final div = _div()..className = 'erreur';
    div.textContent = message;
    return div;
  }

  // a form field [label + champ texte/mot de passe/nombre]
  (web.HTMLDivElement ligne, web.HTMLInputElement input) _ligneChamp(
    String libelle,
    String type,
    String valeurInitiale, {
    String? aide,
  }) {
    final ligne = _div()..className = 'ligne-champ';
    final label = web.document.createElement('label') as web.HTMLLabelElement;
    label.textContent = libelle;
    final champ = _div()..className = 'champ';
    final input = web.document.createElement('input') as web.HTMLInputElement;
    input.type = type;
    input.value = valeurInitiale;
    if (type == 'number') {
      input.min = '0';
    }
    champ.appendChild(input);
    if (aide != null) {
      final div = _div()..className = 'aide';
      div.textContent = aide;
      champ.appendChild(div);
    }
    ligne
      ..appendChild(label)
      ..appendChild(champ);
    return (ligne, input);
  }

  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  // view [authentification]
  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  void vueAuthentification(String? erreur, CallbacksAuthentification callbacks) {
    _viderMenu();
    _contenu.innerHTML = ''.toJS;

    final titre = _div()
      ..className = 'titre-section'
      ..textContent = 'Veuillez vous authentifier';
    _contenu.appendChild(titre);

    final banniere = _banniereErreur(erreur);
    if (banniere != null) _contenu.appendChild(banniere);

    final champUser = _ligneChamp("Nom d'utilisateur", 'text', 'admin');
    final champPassword = _ligneChamp('Mot de passe', 'password', '');
    _contenu
      ..appendChild(champUser.$1)
      ..appendChild(champPassword.$1);

    final bouton = web.document.createElement('button') as web.HTMLButtonElement;
    bouton.textContent = 'Valider';
    bouton.addEventListener(
      'click',
      ((web.Event event) {
        callbacks.onValider(champUser.$2.value.trim(), champPassword.$2.value);
      }).toJS,
    );
    _contenu.appendChild(bouton);
  }

  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  // view [calcul de l'impôt]
  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  void vueCalcul(Simulation? resultat, String? erreur, CallbacksCalcul callbacks) {
    _afficherMenu([
      _lienMenu('Liste des simulations', callbacks.onListe),
      _lienMenu('Fin de session', callbacks.onFinSession),
    ]);

    _contenu.innerHTML = ''.toJS;

    final titre = _div()
      ..className = 'titre-section'
      ..textContent = 'Remplissez le formulaire ci-dessous puis validez-le';
    _contenu.appendChild(titre);

    final banniere = _banniereErreur(erreur);
    if (banniere != null) _contenu.appendChild(banniere);

    // radio line [marié(e)]
    final ligneMarie = _div()..className = 'ligne-champ';
    final labelMarie = web.document.createElement('label') as web.HTMLLabelElement;
    labelMarie.textContent = 'Etes-vous marié(e) ou pacsé(e) ?';
    final champMarie = _div()..className = 'champ radios';

    final radioOui = web.document.createElement('input') as web.HTMLInputElement;
    radioOui.type = 'radio';
    radioOui.name = 'marie';
    radioOui.value = 'oui';
    radioOui.checked = true;
    final labelOui = web.document.createElement('label') as web.HTMLLabelElement;
    labelOui.appendChild(radioOui);
    labelOui.appendChild(web.document.createTextNode(' Oui'));

    final radioNon = web.document.createElement('input') as web.HTMLInputElement;
    radioNon.type = 'radio';
    radioNon.name = 'marie';
    radioNon.value = 'non';
    final labelNon = web.document.createElement('label') as web.HTMLLabelElement;
    labelNon.appendChild(radioNon);
    labelNon.appendChild(web.document.createTextNode(' Non'));

    champMarie
      ..appendChild(labelOui)
      ..appendChild(labelNon);
    ligneMarie
      ..appendChild(labelMarie)
      ..appendChild(champMarie);
    _contenu.appendChild(ligneMarie);

    final champEnfants = _ligneChamp("Nombre d'enfants à charge", 'number', '0');
    _contenu.appendChild(champEnfants.$1);

    final champSalaire = _ligneChamp(
      'Salaire annuel',
      'number',
      '',
      aide: "Arrondissez à l'euro inférieur",
    );
    _contenu.appendChild(champSalaire.$1);

    final bouton = web.document.createElement('button') as web.HTMLButtonElement;
    bouton.textContent = 'Valider';
    bouton.addEventListener(
      'click',
      ((web.Event event) {
        final marie = radioOui.checked ? 'oui' : 'non';
        final enfants = int.tryParse(champEnfants.$2.value) ?? 0;
        final salaire = int.tryParse(champSalaire.$2.value) ?? 0;
        callbacks.onValider(marie, enfants, salaire);
      }).toJS,
    );
    _contenu.appendChild(bouton);

    // result of the latest simulation (green box), if any
    if (resultat != null) {
      final box = _div()..className = 'resultat';
      final tauxPourcent = (resultat.taux * 100).round();
      box.innerHTML = ("Montant de l'impôt : ${resultat.impot} euros<br>"
              "Décôte : ${resultat.decote} euros<br>"
              "Réduction : ${resultat.reduction} euros<br>"
              "Surcôte : ${resultat.surcote} euros<br>"
              "Taux d'imposition : $tauxPourcent %")
          .toJS;
      _contenu.appendChild(box);
    }
  }

  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  // view [liste des simulations]
  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  void vueListe(List<Simulation> simulations, String? erreur, CallbacksListe callbacks) {
    _afficherMenu([
      _lienMenu("Calcul de l'impôt", callbacks.onCalcul),
      _lienMenu('Fin de session', callbacks.onFinSession),
    ]);

    _contenu.innerHTML = ''.toJS;

    final titre = _div()
      ..className = 'titre-section'
      ..textContent = 'Liste de vos simulations';
    _contenu.appendChild(titre);

    final banniere = _banniereErreur(erreur);
    if (banniere != null) _contenu.appendChild(banniere);

    if (simulations.isEmpty) {
      final vide = _div()
        ..className = 'simulations-vide'
        ..textContent = 'Aucune simulation enregistrée.';
      _contenu.appendChild(vide);
      return;
    }

    final table = web.document.createElement('table') as web.HTMLTableElement;
    table.className = 'simulations';
    final thead = web.document.createElement('thead') as web.HTMLTableSectionElement;
    thead.innerHTML = ("<tr><th>#</th><th>Marié</th><th>Nombre d'enfants</th>"
            "<th>Salaire annuel</th><th>Montant impôt</th><th>Surcôte</th>"
            "<th>Décôte</th><th>Réduction</th><th>Taux</th><th></th></tr>")
        .toJS;
    table.appendChild(thead);

    final tbody = web.document.createElement('tbody') as web.HTMLTableSectionElement;
    for (var numero = 0; numero < simulations.length; numero++) {
      final simulation = simulations[numero];
      final tr = web.document.createElement('tr') as web.HTMLTableRowElement;
      final tauxPourcent = (simulation.taux * 100).round();
      tr.innerHTML = ("<td>$numero</td>"
              "<td>${simulation.marie}</td>"
              "<td>${simulation.enfants}</td>"
              "<td>${simulation.salaire}</td>"
              "<td>${simulation.impot}</td>"
              "<td>${simulation.surcote}</td>"
              "<td>${simulation.decote}</td>"
              "<td>${simulation.reduction}</td>"
              "<td>$tauxPourcent %</td>")
          .toJS;
      final tdSupprimer = web.document.createElement('td') as web.HTMLTableCellElement;
      final lienSupprimer = web.document.createElement('a') as web.HTMLAnchorElement;
      lienSupprimer.className = 'supprimer';
      lienSupprimer.textContent = 'Supprimer';
      lienSupprimer.addEventListener(
        'click',
        ((web.Event event) => callbacks.onSupprimer(numero)).toJS,
      );
      tdSupprimer.appendChild(lienSupprimer);
      tr.appendChild(tdSupprimer);
      tbody.appendChild(tr);
    }
    table.appendChild(tbody);
    _contenu.appendChild(table);
  }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 19: [import 'package:web/web.dart' as web;]: the modern replacement for the old [dart:html], with a API and DOM very similar to the standard DOM used by Vues.ts ([document.createElement], [.textContent], [.addEventListener]...).
  • Lines 44–45: [typedef CallbacksCalcul = ({void Function(...) onValider, ...});]: A TypeScript callback interface naturally translates to a RECORD, DE, and FONCTIONS in Dart 3—lighter than a class for a simple group of functions.
  • Line 108: [a.addEventListener('click', ((web.Event event) { ... }).toJS);]: A Dart event handler (a simple function) must be converted to the function JavaScript using [.toJS] (an extension of [dart:js_interop]) before being passed to [addEventListener] - the “bridge” between the Dart world and the JavaScript world is made explicit, whereas TypeScript requires no conversion.
  • line 141: [input.value = valeurInitiale;], [titre.textContent = '...';] (line 76): most string-type properties remain simple Dart strings, with no conversion required. [innerHTML] becomes EXCEPTION: [dart analyze] signals this if a [String] is assigned to it directly—its setter expects a [JSAny] (a peculiarity of its generation, related to the WebIDL [LegacyNullToEmptyString] attribute of the standard DOM)—hence [racine.innerHTML = ''.toJS;]: an additional [.toJS] conversion, beyond the functions alone, which must be kept in mind whenever handling [innerHTML].
  • line 129: [(web.HTMLDivElement ligne, web.HTMLInputElement input) _ligneChamp(...)]: a positional RECORD as the return type, to return two DOM elements at once without an intermediate class—yet another practical use of Dart 3 records.

docs.title: 6.5.8. [app_html] script
docs.text:
// app_html.dart
// Port AppHtml.ts: the HTML application controller. It orchestrates the
// server calls ([dao] layer, dao3.dart layer), calculations (
// [métier], metier.dart) and the display of views (layer [vues],
// vues.dart).
//
// Like main3.dart, this client only makes requests to the server NestJS for three
// actions: [init-session], [authentifier-utilisateur], and [get-admindata].
// Once the tax data (rates, thresholds, etc.) has been retrieved using
// [get-admindata], the [métier] layer calculates the tax in the
// browser, without making another network request. Is the list of simulations
// also stored solely in the browser (field [simulations]),
// exactly as main3.dart does with its local variable
// [simulations] (`simulations.add(...)`, `simulations.removeAt(...)`).
import 'dart:js_interop';
import 'package:http/browser_client.dart';
import 'dao3.dart';
import 'metier.dart';
import 'simulation.dart';
import 'vues.dart';
import 'package:web/web.dart' as web;

class AppHtml {
  final Dao3 dao;
  final Vues vues;
  // [métier] layer: exists only after tax data has been retrieved
  // (after successful authentication) — see [initialiserMetier]. A
  // field NULLABLE (Occupation?), not a late field ([late]): unlike
  // to Vues.ts, where [métier?: Métier] simply remains "undefined" as long as
  // is not assigned, a Dart field named [late] would throw an error if it were
  // LISAIT before assignment (which is exactly what [finSession] does by
  // and thereby nulling it)—so the nullable type is the right choice here, not
  // just a matter of style.
  Metier? _metier;
  // list of simulations already calculated, stored in the browser
  List<Simulation> _simulations = [];

  // [différence avec TypeScript] AppHtml.ts configures an instance GLOBALE
  // from Axios (axios.defaults.timeout/baseURL/withCredentials) and then passes it
  // to the Dao. Here, [BrowserClient] (package:http/browser_client.dart, previously
  // encountered in main3.dart) carries the equivalent of
  // "axios.defaults.withCredentials = true"; there is no equivalent
  // that directly corresponds to a “global timeout” on http.Client—it would be applied on a case-by-case basis
  // on a case-by-case basis with `.timeout(Duration(...))` on each call, as in the
  // chapter [http] (dart_fetch_01.dart).
  AppHtml()
      : dao = Dao3(
          BrowserClient()..withCredentials = true,
          'http://localhost:3000',
        ),
        vues = Vues(web.document.getElementById('app') as web.HTMLElement);

  // application entry point
  Future<void> demarrer() async {
    try {
      // init session—required before any other action (see main.php)
      final reponse = await dao.initSession() as Map<String, dynamic>;
      if (reponse['état'] != 700) {
        vues.vueAuthentification(
          _formaterErreur(reponse['réponse']),
          (onValider: (user, password) => _authentifier(user, password)),
        );
        return;
      }
    } catch (erreur) {
      vues.vueAuthentification(
        "Impossible de contacter le serveur ($erreur)",
        (onValider: (user, password) => _authentifier(user, password)),
      );
      return;
    }
    // session initialized: display authentication
    _afficherAuthentification();
  }

  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  // view [authentification]
  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  void _afficherAuthentification([String? erreur]) {
    vues.vueAuthentification(
      erreur,
      (onValider: (user, password) => _authentifier(user, password)),
    );
  }

  Future<void> _authentifier(String user, String password) async {
    try {
      final reponse = await dao.authentifierUtilisateur(user, password)
          as Map<String, dynamic>;
      if (reponse['état'] == 200) {
        // Authentication successful: as in main3.dart, we retrieve
        // now, once and for all, the tax data
        // required by the layer [métier]
        await _initialiserMetier();
      } else {
        // failure (incorrect username/password, or missing parameters)
        _afficherAuthentification(_formaterErreur(reponse['réponse']));
      }
    } catch (erreur) {
      _afficherAuthentification("Impossible de contacter le serveur ($erreur)");
    }
  }

  // retrieves data from the tax authority and instantiates the
  // [métier] layer with this data—a single server call for the entire
  // session, exactly like main3.dart
  Future<void> _initialiserMetier() async {
    try {
      final reponse = await dao.getAdminData() as Map<String, dynamic>;
      if (reponse['état'] == 1000) {
        _metier = Metier(reponse['réponse'] as Map<String, dynamic>);
        // new work session: we start with an empty list
        _simulations = [];
        _afficherCalcul();
      } else {
        _afficherAuthentification(_formaterErreur(reponse['réponse']));
      }
    } catch (erreur) {
      _afficherAuthentification("Impossible de contacter le serveur ($erreur)");
    }
  }

  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  // view [calcul de l'impôt]
  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  void _afficherCalcul([Simulation? resultat, String? erreur]) {
    vues.vueCalcul(
      resultat,
      erreur,
      (
        onValider: (marie, enfants, salaire) =>
            _calculer(marie, enfants, salaire),
        onListe: () => _afficherListe(),
        onFinSession: () => _finSession(),
      ),
    );
  }

  // Tax calculation performed entirely in the browser (layer
  // [métier]): no server calls, unlike the first version
  // of this client (HTTP client 1 / HTTP client 2)
  void _calculer(String marie, int enfants, int salaire) {
    // _metier must have been initialized: the [calcul] view
    // only after _initialiserMetier (so [!] is definitely here, as is [!]
    // from TypeScript to [this.métier!])
    final resultat = _metier!.calculerImpot(marie, enfants, salaire);
    // [différence avec TypeScript] Vues.ts builds the simulation with a
    // simple object spread: `{ married, children, salary, ...result }`.
    // Here, [Simulation] is a RECORD (simulation.dart), not a Map: a
    // record cannot be “populated” via spread from a Map, and
    // its fields are named SANS with accents (tax, surcharge, etc.), whereas
    // [resultat], returned by metier.dart, is a Map whose keys
    // GARDENT contain accents (“impôt,” “surcôte,” etc.; see metier.dart). We
    // thus reconstructs the record field by field—a bit more verbose
    // than a spread, but fully verified by the compiler (a
    // is a compilation error, not a surprise at
    // runtime).
    final Simulation simulation = (
      marie: marie,
      enfants: enfants,
      salaire: salaire,
      impot: resultat['impôt'] as num,
      surcote: resultat['surcôte'] as num,
      decote: resultat['décôte'] as num,
      reduction: resultat['réduction'] as num,
      taux: resultat['taux'] as num,
    );
    // stored in the browser (such as `simulations.add(...)` in
    // main3.dart)
    _simulations.add(simulation);
    _afficherCalcul(simulation);
  }

  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  // view [liste des simulations]
  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  // No more server calls here: the list is already entirely in
  // [_simulations]
  void _afficherListe([String? erreur]) {
    vues.vueListe(
      _simulations,
      erreur,
      (
        onSupprimer: (numero) => _supprimer(numero),
        onCalcul: () => _afficherCalcul(),
        onFinSession: () => _finSession(),
      ),
    );
  }

  void _supprimer(int numero) {
    // local deletion of [_simulations], as
    // `simulations.removeAt(number)` in main3.dart - still none
    // server call
    _simulations.removeAt(numero);
    _afficherListe();
  }

  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  // end of session
  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  void _finSession() {
    // end of session on the client side only: we ignore the [métier] layer
    // (i.e., tax data) and the simulations already calculated, then
    // return to the authentication screen. This client does not need to
    // to query the server for this.
    _metier = null;
    _simulations = [];
    _afficherAuthentification();
  }

  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  // formats the field [réponse] from a server error response, which
  // is either a string or a list of strings (see PHP controllers)
  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
  String _formaterErreur(Object? reponse) {
    if (reponse is List) {
      return reponse.join(' ; ');
    }
    return '$reponse';
  }
}

// execution—[différence avec TypeScript] the event handler
// passed to addEventListener must be converted to function JavaScript with
// [.toJS] (see vues.dart); this is only the "entry point" version of
//—the same rule.
void main() {
  web.window.addEventListener(
    'DOMContentLoaded',
    ((web.Event event) {
      AppHtml().demarrer();
    }).toJS,
  );
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 46–51: [AppHtml() : dao = Dao3(BrowserClient()..withCredentials = true, ...), vues = Vues(...)]: constructing DAO and VUES from a LISTE built from INITIALISATION - Same concept as the TypeScript constructor, using the Dart-specific [: champ1 = ..., champ2 = ...] syntax.
  • Line 34: [Metier? _metier;]: a NULLABLE field, where AppHtml.ts previously used [métier?: Métier] - the same concept (“not yet initialized”), using the same [!] operator to confirm that it is indeed populated at a specific point in the code.
  • Lines 158–162: [final Simulation simulation = (marie: marie, ..., impot: resultat['impôt'] as num, ...);]: unlike the simple spread [{ marié, enfants, salaire, ...résultat }] from Vues.ts, a RECORD cannot be completed by a spread from a [Map] - the record is therefore reconstructed as CHAMP PAR CHAMP, which is slightly more verbose but fully validated by the compiler.
  • Lines 229–233: [web.window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', ((web.Event event) { AppHtml().demarrer(); }).toJS);]: the same entry point as AppHtml.ts, with the same callback conversion ([.toJS]) as in vues.dart.

docs.title: 6.5.9. Compilation and Execution
docs.text:
See README.md in this folder: [dart pub get] followed by [webdev serve] for development (including hot reloading), or [dart compile js web/main.dart -o web/main.dart.js] for a production build—the Dart equivalent of [npm run build], without any prior bundler configuration steps.

If the [webserve] server is still running for the [client http3] web application, you must stop it (Ctrl-C in the terminal that launched it). Then, in a terminal within the [client html] directory:

dart pub get
webdev serve

Line 2 starts the web server that will serve the HTML client application:

  • In [1], in a browser, request URL and [http://localhost:8080];
  • to [2-3], enter the credentials admin / admin;
  • In [4], submit the page;

  • In [2], fill in the fields;
  • In [3], submit the page;

The tax amount is displayed in [1]. Run several simulations, then request the list in [2];

  • In [1], delete a simulation;

  • in [1], end the session;

docs.title: 6.6. Conclusion
docs.text: The four clients in this chapter illustrate, with Dart, exactly the same progression as with TypeScript: from server-side processing to client-side processing, then from the CLI script to the full web client. The key differences to note are the manual tracking of the session cookie (necessary in CLI, unnecessary in a browser), the [.toJS] conversion enforced by [dart:js_interop] to bridge the Dart/JavaScript boundary in views, and the complete absence of polyfills during web compilation—a clear advantage of the Dart toolchain over the webpack/babel pipeline.

docs.title: 4. Installing a NestJS Server
docs.text:
This chapter is reproduced verbatim from the TypeScript course: installing a web server is not specific to any particular client language, and the server installed here serves as a common target for both courses. The only difference is that the numerous screenshots from the TypeScript document (installation of Laragon, HeidiSQL, Postman—a good hundred images in total) are not reproduced here; the text, however, is reproduced in its entirety. For step-by-step visual instructions, refer to document [Introduction au langage TypeScript et au framework NestJS], which describes the exact same installation.

Note: In the following, reference is sometimes made to a server PHP, the one referenced in the course [Introduction au langage PHP7 par l'exemple]. The server NestJS implements the same services as this server PHP.

We will cover the HTTP functions in Dart, which allow you to query a web server. For our tests, we need a web server. We will use the one developed for the TypeScript course (Chapter [Étude de cas : le serveur de calcul de l'impôt en NestJS], not covered in this course but whose server is still used as a target). This server hosts a jSON service offering the following services:

  • [init-session] - GET [main.php?action=init-session&type=json] - tells the server that we want responses from jSON;
  • [authentifier-utilisateur] - POST [main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur]: the two posted parameters [user, password] determine whether or not to allow connection to the service jSON. By default, the credentials are [admin, admin];
  • [calculer-impot] - POST [main.php?action=calculer-impot]: The posted parameters [marié, enfants, salaire] are used to calculate a tax ([marié]: “yes” or “no,” [enfants]: number of the taxpayer’s children, [salaire]: the taxpayer’s annual salary);
  • [lister-simulations] - GET [main.php?action=lister-simulations] - lists the simulations performed since the start of the session;
  • [supprimer-simulation] - GET [main.php?action=supprimer-simulation&numéro=x] - removes simulation No. x from the list of simulations;
  • [get-admindata] - GET [main.php?action=get-admindata] - retrieves the entire database associated with the server into an object named jSON;
  • [fin-session] - GET [main.php?action=fin-session]: ends the session. To start another session, the user must issue the “init-session” command above.

docs.title: 4.1. Installing Laragon
docs.text:
In September 2026, the Laragon tool is available at URL [Download Laragon – Fast & Modern Dev Environment ]. Laragon includes tools that allow you to install a PHP server and the SGBD MySQL:

  • in [1], an Apache web server;
  • into [2], the SGBD and MySQL;
  • to [3], a messaging tool that we will not be using;
  • [4] starts all services (Apache, MySQL, MailPit);
  • [5] displays the web page for URL and [http://localhost]. By default, this URL refers to the <laragon-install>\www folder, where <laragon-install> is the Laragon installation folder;
  • in [6], launches the HeidiSQL tool, which allows you to manage MySQL databases. We will use this tool to create the database used by the tax calculation server;
  • In [7], open a terminal; all the binaries needed for Laragon are located in PATH;
  • In [8], open a Windows Explorer window in the folder associated with URL and [http://localhost];

The Laragon installation folder contains the following items:

  • In [1], the [bin] folder contains numerous applications:
  • In [1], the Apache web server;
  • in [2], a command-line terminal;
  • in [3], a client for [git] that allows you to manage different versions of a project;
  • in [4], a database manager;
  • [5], an email manager;
  • in [6], the SGBD and MySQL;
  • [7], another web server;
  • in [8], [node.js] to run JavaScript scripts;
  • [9], a text editor;
  • [10], the PHP interpreter;
  • [11], the [Python] interpreter;
  • [12], a cache server;

Laragon comes with a comprehensive development environment. In this course, we will only use SGBD, MySQL, [6], and [heidisql] to manage it graphically;

docs.title: 4.2. Installation and Configuration of the NestJS Server
docs.text:
A NestJS server for a highly simplified tax calculation can be found in the nestjs-etude-de-cas folder within the script directory for this course:


nestjs-etude-de-cas/
├── package.json
├── nest-cli.json
├── .env.example
├── create_dbimpots.sql
├── src/
│   ├── main.ts
│   ├── main.controller.ts
│   ├── app.module.ts
│   ├── actions/
│   ├── config/
│   ├── entities/
│   ├── filters/
│   ├── model/
│   ├── responses/
│   ├── session/
│   └── utilities/
└── views/

If you have already installed the dependencies for the entire directory tree (using npm install at the root directory, via the npm workspaces described in the introduction to this document), the nestjs-case-study folder already contains its node\_modules. Otherwise, navigate to that folder and run:

npm install
Note: If you followed the batch installation described in the introduction (running `npm install` at the root of `cours-typescript-nestjs-scripts`), this step is already complete: proceed directly to the configuration below.

The server needs a .env file to specify the connection settings for the MySQL database created by Laragon (see above) as well as the listening port. Copy the provided .env.example file to .env and modify it as follows:

PORT=3000
TAX_DATA_SOURCE=mysql
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=3306
DB_NAME=dbimpots-2019
DB_USER=admimpots
DB_PASSWORD=mdpimpots
CORS_ALLOWED=true
SESSION_SECRET=change-moi-en-production
  • PORT: the listening port for the NestJS server (default is 3000).
  • TAX_DATA_SOURCE: MySQL to use the database created below;
  • DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD: the connection parameters for the dbimpots-2019 database that we will create with HeidiSQL (see below)—same credentials as those defined in the create_dbimpots.sql script shown in the directory tree above;
  • CORS_ALLOWED: allows calls to CORS from a TypeScript client running on a different port.
  • SESSION_SECRET: the key used to sign the session cookie—change it if the server is ever to be made publicly accessible.

docs.title: 4.3. Creating the Database
docs.text:
To create the MySQL database required by the NestJS server, we use a Laragon option:

  • In [1], all services must be started;
  • in [2], the [Database] option allows you to manage the database;

The [Database] option launches a utility called HeidiSQL:

  • In [1], you can select various SGBD options. The default value provided is SGBD MySQL. This is acceptable;
  • in [2], you log in to HeidiSQL;
  • In [1-2], run the SQL file, then select the [create_dbimpots.sql] file, which you’ll find in the [nestjs-etude-de-cas] folder:

Running the [2] file will create the [dbimpots-2019] database used by the tax calculation server. To view it, run F5 within HeidiSQL to refresh the display:

The database [dbimpots-2019] has been created.

docs.title: 4.4. Starting the NestJS server
docs.text:
Once the .env file is in place (and the database has been created), open a terminal at the root of the [nestjs-etude-de-cas] folder, then compile and start the server:

npm run build
npm run start:prod

For development, with automatic restart after every source code change, use:

npm run start:dev

In both cases, the console displays:

[Nest] ... [NestFactory] Starting Nest application...
[Nest] ... [InstanceLoader] AppModule dependencies initialized
[Nest] ... [RoutesResolver] MainController {/}:
[Nest] ... [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/main.php, ALL} route
[Nest] ... [NestApplication] Nest application successfully started
Serveur de calcul de l’impôt (NestJS) démarré sur http://localhost:3000
Point d’entrée jSON : http://localhost:3000/main.php?action=init-session&type=json
Point d’entrée HTML : http://localhost:3000/main.php?action=init-session&type=html

The NestJS server has a single entry point (main.php, retained for compatibility even though it is actually NestJS) that receives all requests, and an “action” request parameter that selects the processing to be performed:

docs.title: 4.5. HTML tests for the tax calculation server
docs.text:
If you haven't already, start all Laragon services (for MySQL) as well as the NestJS server (npm run start:prod or npm run start:dev; see above). Then, in a browser, request the URL at http://localhost:3000/main.php?action=init-session&type=html — this is the same init-session action as for the PHP server, with the same type=html parameter, but on port 3000:

The credentials are admin/admin, exactly the same as for the PHP server—they are defined in the same way, in the server code rather than in config.json. Enter them:

Fill out the form and then submit it. You’ll see the following page:

The tax calculation result is displayed—this page is indeed using the database we just created. The “List of Simulations” link in the left-hand menu displays the history of calculations for this session:

If you get these results, the NestJS tax calculation server is working correctly with its MySQL database. We are now ready to query the server with TypeScript clients. To do this, we will use version jSON of the server.

docs.title: 4.6. The API and jSON versions of the tax calculation server
4.6.1. Postman Tests
docs.text:
The PHP server was tested using the Postman desktop tool. The same collection of requests (impots-servers-tests.postman_collection.json, provided in the netjs-cours folder) works identically against the NestJS server: API and jSON are exactly the same—same actions, same parameters, same status codes. In Postman, simply change the port for each request (80 → 3000), or more simply, the base URL in the collection if you’ve defined it as a variable.

The Postman tool is available at URL [https://www.postman.com/downloads/]. You may need to create an account.

Start all Laragon services, then open the Postman desktop app:

  • In [1-2], create a request HTTP to query the tax calculation server;
  • In [1], you can name your query HTTP. You will be able to save it and retrieve it;
  • In [2]: enter the URL of the server you want to query;
  • In [3]: select the query type HTTP. We’ll use two of them in the following: GET and POST;
  • in [4]: if your query has parameters of the type [?param1=val1&param2=val2&…], you can define them here;
  • in [5]: if the query type is POST, this is where you define the posted values;

In [nestjs-cours], you will find a collection of HTTP requests to the tax calculation server that you can import into POSTMAN.

Proceed as follows. In Postman, run [Ctrl-O]:

  • Use the link [1] to import the file [impots-servers-tests.postman_collection.json] from the folder [netjs-cours]:
  • In [1], the name of the imported collection;
  • in [2], its contents. This is a list of requests (HTTP) to the tax calculation server (jSON);

Let’s look, for example, at the request named [init-session-json-700]. It initiates a session jSON with the server:

  • In [1], the request HTTP is a GET;
  • in [2], the queried URL. It requests to initiate a jSON dialogue with the server;
  • in [3-4], we find the parameters from GET;
  • in [5], to send the request to the tax calculation server;

Before sending the request, make sure you have started the Laragon services. The server’s response, jSON, is as follows:

Now use the request named [init-session-703]:

The request [1-3] is invalid. The parameters must be of the type [?action=xx&type=yy], where “type” can be “html,” “xml,” or “json.” The type “x” will not be recognized. The server’s response, jSON, is as follows:

Resend the request [init-session-json-700] to restart a session jSON. Then send the request [authentifier-utilisateur-200] to authenticate yourself:

  • In [1], the request is POST;
  • in [2], the authentication request URL;
  • in [3], the body of POST, which contains the posted values;
  • [4-5], the two posted values. These are the application administrator’s credentials. They are defined in the server’s [config.service.ts] file;

The server’s response, jSON, is as follows:

Once you are authenticated, you can perform a tax calculation. To do so, use the query [calculer-impot-300]:

  • In [1], this is a POST request;
  • in [2], the URL query is called;
  • in [3-4], the three values are posted;

The response jSON is as follows:

Run the request several times, changing the posted values each time. Once you’ve done that, run the request [lister-simulations], which will display the list of simulations you’ve performed:

  • The request GET [1-4] has only one parameter: [action]. The response jSON is as follows:

This is the list of simulations you have performed.

Use the query [supprimer-simulation-600] to delete a simulation:

  • In [2], the URL is queried with a GET. It includes two parameters: [action, numéro]. [numéro] is the number of the simulation you want to delete from the list of simulations. Here, the number 0 refers to the first simulation in the list;

The server’s response, jSON, is as follows:

The response jSON is the remaining list of simulations after deleting one of them;

Finally, you can end the session with the query [fin-session-400]:

The query URL [1-2] has only the parameter [action] (3). The response jSON is as follows:

docs.title: 4.6.2. curl Tests
docs.text:
We can also use the [curl] tool to test the server’s jSON services. All of the following requests use the same session, HTTP (the -b/-c cookies.txt option in curl preserves the session cookie between calls, just as a browser or Postman would):

Let’s start a jSON session with the [init-session] action:

curl -c cookies.txt "http://localhost:3000/main.php?action=init-session&type=json"

{
  "action": "init-session",
  "état": 700,
  "réponse": "session démarrée avec type [json]"
}

Status code 700 confirms that the session has started—this is the same code that the server returned: PHP. Now let’s authenticate using the [authentifier-utilisateur] action—a POST request, with a single parameter in the URL (action) and the credentials posted:

curl -b cookies.txt -c cookies.txt -X POST "http://localhost:3000/main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur" \
     -d "user=admin&password=admin"

{
  "action": "authentifier-utilisateur",
  "état": 200,
  "réponse": "Authentification réussie [admin, admin]"
}

You can now calculate taxes using transaction [calculer-impot], or continue using POST with the three posted parameters: marital status, children, and salary:

curl -b cookies.txt -c cookies.txt -X POST "http://localhost:3000/main.php?action=calculer-impot" \
     -d "marié=oui&enfants=2&salaire=45000"

{
  "action": "calculer-impot",
  "état": 300,
  "réponse": {
    "marié": "oui",
    "enfants": 2,
    "salaire": 45000,
    "impôt": 502,
    "surcôte": 0,
    "décôte": 857,
    "réduction": 126,
    "taux": 0.14
  }
}

The values are exactly the same (€502 in tax, a discount of €857, a reduction of 126 €, and a rate of 14%) as those displayed in the browser in the previous section—the two versions, HTML and jSON, share the same calculation engine. The list of simulations is obtained using action [lister-simulations], a simple GET:

curl -b cookies.txt -c cookies.txt "http://localhost:3000/main.php?action=lister-simulations"

{
  "action": "lister-simulations",
  "état": 500,
  "réponse": [
    {
      "marié": "oui", "enfants": 2, "salaire": 45000,
      "impôt": 502, "surcôte": 0, "décôte": 857, "réduction": 126, "taux": 0.14
    }
  ]
}

Run the query [calculer-impot] several times by changing the posted values, then use [supprimer-simulation] to remove a simulation from the list (&number=x refers to its sequence number), and [get-admindata] to retrieve the entire database in the format jSON (tax brackets and calculation constants). Finally, end the session with the action [fin-session]:

curl -b cookies.txt -c cookies.txt "http://localhost:3000/main.php?action=fin-session"

{
  "action": "fin-session",
  "état": 400,
  "réponse": "session supprimée"
}

You now have a good understanding of the API and jSON exposed by the NestJS tax calculation server—which is exactly the same as that of the PHP server. We can now move on to writing TypeScript scripts that query this server.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
The document’s PDF is |HERE|.

The document’s codes are |HERE|.

This document is a product of Anthropic’s Claude IA. Its purpose is to transpose the document [Introduction au langage TypeScript et au framework NestJS] by replacing the TypeScript language with the Dart language.

The Anthropic Claude model IA did the bulk of the work (90%):

  • Code generation: Claude generated all of the code. I simply tested it by following the generated course. No Dart was available in the environment where Claude worked (unlike in the TypeScript course, where each script could be executed and verified by Claude): the scripts for this course were written and reviewed with the same care, checked for syntax (balanced curly braces and parentheses, presence of a [main] entry point in each executable script), but could not be compiled or executed prior to delivery. Note: All delivered code was tested by the course reviewer. Errors were reported to Claude, who corrected them immediately.
  • Course generation in ODT format: Claude generated several versions at my request. This is where I was primarily involved.

Serge Tahé, September 2026

==

This document is an introductory course on the [Dart] language, designed on the same principle as the [Introduction to the TypeScript language and the NestJS web framework through examples (2026)] course: learning a language through a series of small, standalone scripts, commented line by line, rather than through a theoretical exposition of its grammar.

The progression follows exactly that of the TypeScript course: the same concepts, in the same order, with a Dart script alongside each TypeScript script. This symmetry is intentional: it allows you, at any time, to directly compare how Dart and TypeScript address the same need—and to identify, for each difference, what stems from a simple choice of syntax and what stems from a fundamental difference between the two languages (structural typing versus nominal typing, compilation versus transpilation, the presence or absence of implicit coercion, etc.).

Two chapters from the TypeScript course have been intentionally omitted here: PAS, [Introduction au framework Web NestJS], and [Étude de cas : le serveur de calcul de l'impôt en NestJS]. These two chapters cover a server-side web framework written in TypeScript—a topic not directly related to learning the Dart language itself. The NestJS tax calculation server, on the other hand, is retained: once installed (see the chapter “Installing a NestJS Server”), it serves as a real-world target for testing Dart functions—exactly as it serves as a target for the HTTP and TypeScript clients from the original course.

However, a difference in scope distinguishes this course from course TypeScript: the [Les fondamentaux] section of course TypeScript devotes three entire sections to recent updates to ECMAScript (2020–2024, 2026) and to API and [Temporal]. These new features are specific to JavaScript/TypeScript and have no direct equivalent in Dart; they are replaced here by a section on [Nouveautés Dart 3.x], dedicated to recent features specific to Dart: [records], [pattern matching], [sealed] classes, and class modifiers.

docs.title: 1.1. Target Audience and Prerequisites
docs.text:
This course is intended for readers who are already familiar with programming—ideally, those who have already taken the TypeScript course, since the constant comparison between the two languages is central to the teaching approach used here. No prior knowledge of Dart is required: each new concept is introduced through a minimal script, commented on in detail.

Contrary to the common misconception that reduces Dart to “the language of Flutter,” this course does not mention Flutter or mobile interfaces at any point: Dart is used here as a general-purpose programming language, run from the command line ([dart run]), exactly as TypeScript was used with [tsx] in the original course.

docs.title: 1.2. Organization of the Sample Project
docs.text:
The scripts for this course are provided in a separate directory structure, [dart-fondamentaux/], which mirrors the folder structure of the TypeScript course ([bases/], [tableaux/], [objets/], [strings/], [regexp/], [fonctions/], [exceptions/], [modules/], [async/], [classes/], [http/]...), plus a new folder, [dart3/], for the [Nouveautés Dart 3.x] section. A second directory tree, [dart-bases-de-donnees/], contains the “Database Access” chapter. Each folder contains its own [README.md] and, when necessary, its own [pubspec.yaml] (the Dart equivalent of [package.json] from Node.js; see the following chapter).

Each script is run individually using the command [dart run], followed by the script’s path—for example, [dart run dart-fondamentaux/bases/bases_01.dart]. No full installation of the project is required to run a single script: [dart pub get] (equivalent to [npm install]), run once at the root of a folder containing a [pubspec.yaml], is sufficient to install the dependencies for all the scripts it contains.

docs.title: 2. Setting Up a Development Environment
docs.text:
Note: In the following steps, we’ll use the VSCode tool to test the Dart scripts. Open two VSCode windows and use [File / Open Folder] to open the folders for both projects.

The TypeScript course installs Node.js, an npm project ([package.json]), TypeScript itself and its type checker ([tsc]), a script runner that does not require prior compilation ([tsx]), and finally ESLint. The Dart equivalent of this entire toolchain consists of a single component to install: [SDK Dart]—which can be downloaded from [dart.dev] or, more simply, installed via a system package manager ([choco install dart-sdk] on Windows, [brew install dart] on macOS, or the official APT repository on Linux/Debian/Ubuntu).

Whereas TypeScript requires three separate tools (the [tsc] compiler to check types, [tsx] to run a script without compiling it first, and ESLint for style analysis), the Dart tool SDK provides all of this in a single command, [dart], which includes the following subcommands: [dart run] (runs a script), [dart analyze] (checks the style—the combined equivalent of [tsc], ET, and ESLint), [dart pub] (manages dependencies, equivalent to [npm]), [dart format] (reformats the code, equivalent to Prettier) and [dart test] (runs the tests).

docs.title: 2.1. Verifying Installed Tools
docs.text:
Once SDK is installed, verify the installation in a terminal using VSCode:


PS C:\Data\st-2026\dev\dart\dart-sept-2026-scripts\dart-fondamentaux> dart --version
Dart SDK version: 3.12.2 (stable) (Tue Jun 9 01:11:39 2026 -0700) on "windows_x64"

which displays the version of SDK (for example, [Dart SDK version: 3.5.0 (stable)]). Unlike Node.js and TypeScript, which are installed separately (one version of Node, one version of TypeScript), the version number of SDK Dart covers the language, the compiler, and all the tools controlled by [dart]: there is only one version to track.

docs.title: 2.2. Setting up the VSCode project
docs.text: As with TypeScript, create a project folder and open it in VSCode. Whereas a TypeScript project is declared with two files ([package.json] for dependencies, [tsconfig.json] for compiler options), a Dart project requires only one: [pubspec.yaml].

docs.title: 2.2.1. The pubspec.yaml file
docs.text:
[pubspec.yaml] serves both the role of [package.json] (project name, dependencies) and, to a lesser extent, that of [tsconfig.json] (the key [environment: sdk:] sets the range of accepted SDK Dart versions, much like [target]/[lib] define the version of ECMAScript targeted by [tsc]):
